Consolidation in the Premier League would constitute a successful season for Leeds United, according to former Whites defender Danny Mills.

Leeds sit ninth in the table after 10 games and have taken already taken points off the likes of Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and Brighton & Hove Albion.

Some pundits have suggested the Whites could push for European football, but Mills believes the securing of safety at the earliest point possible takes precedence.

The 49-year-old, who represented Leeds between 1994 and 2004, told BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds: “I think what Leeds did last season was to fall into a formation that worked for them.

“They're high energy, they're aggressive, they're physical, and they've caused teams a lot of problems.

“What would be success for Leeds this season? Safe by March, I would say. The second season in the Premier League, if you can consolidate again, then you start to go, right, okay, now we're here and hopefully here for a while and you build slowly.

It has been revealed that “They did fantastically well last season to stay up. Now you're looking at them going, okay, they're solid. They don't get beat easily. It's a fantastic basis to work from.”.

Leeds have enjoyed success with the use of a flexible 3-4-2-1 formation, with the system spearheaded by talismanic frontman Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

In a recent development, mills said: “They've got a formation that's worked, they've recruited for that formation. They will be difficult to beat, and they will cause teams problems with their athleticism in the wide areas. Dominic Calvert-Lewin up front as well.

Recent findings suggest that “They do have replacements and they might even look in January thinking, ‘okay, it looks like we're gonna be safe’. They might even recruit, you know, whether it be a back-up or someone to assist Dominic Calvert-Lewin in that area. I think they're in a strong position at the moment.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:05 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 15 November 2026.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ mentioned the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and stated: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a massive voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’.

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain.

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order.

It has been revealed that branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander's partnership with assistant Chris Lucketti was a winning one, with coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle also being key components to the Bantams' upturn.

Early days it may be for Duff, but the Bantams chief is quick to value the input of his own number two in Alex Morris and the aforesaid coaching duo who have been stalwarts at the club in recent years.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Duff, whose side are preparing for back-to-back home league derbies with Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley, said: "Truey's been in the club for a long time and worked under a few managers.

"Quite often it can be: 'Oh, here we go, here's another one, what's he going to do, what's he going to say?'.

"But I've had some good conversations with Truey and him and Doyler have been really, really good. But they couldn't beat me and Alex at padel, I'll throw that one in!

Recent findings suggest that "Sometimes, it's little things in training. We review every training session and sometimes it's a case of 'Well, they wouldn't have been used to that because of this' or 'They might not like that because of this'.

"It's like: 'Okay, well that's good to know.' That's where we (Duff and Morris) may need to check ourselves and go: 'Okay, what's the best thing for the team ultimately'.".

Duff and Morris enjoyed a strong working relationship during their time together at previous club Wycombe Wanderers, with Duff moving swiftly to sound out Morris about heading north and renewing their union when the opportunity presented itself at Valley Parade.

He acknowledges that his deputy is particularly notable for daily dialogue with players, as his assistant position allows him to develop a more up-close-and-personal relationship.

According to recent reports, the City boss continued: "Alex spends a lot more time with the players than I do because he's around them a lot more often and they'll probably have more personal conversations with Alex. It's something he's very good at.

Sources indicate that "I try to, but obviously sometimes when you speak to a player, it's like: 'Well, he's the headmaster, so tell him what he wants and get out,' which I don't want it to be like that. But that's just the natural evolution of my job.

"Alex is good for many different reasons. Tactically, he's very, very good and has been coaching for a long, long time.

According to recent reports, "He's coached at a high level. He's worked with League Two players and worked at Championship level, so he can put on different sessions and knows what the group needs and knows me as well.

"Sometimes that's where assistants are really good, because it's like: 'I know you want to do this, but this might not be right at the moment'. And that's where sometimes I have to check my own ego, because it's not about me.

"He's a really good sort of sounding board because he knows me really well.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mauritania and Burkina Faso are back in action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they go head to head at the Stade Cheikha Ould Boidiya on Tuesday evening.
  • With just four points between first and third in the Group F standings midway through the qualifiers, both nations know the result here could prove decisive in shaping their qualification ambitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Ojele | 16 Nov 2026 06:06, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 06:12.

Mauritania and Burkina Faso are back in action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they go head to head at the Stade Cheikha Ould Boidiya on Tuesday evening.

With just four points between first and third in the Group F standings midway through the qualifiers, both nations know the result here could prove decisive in shaping their qualification ambitions.

Having kicked off their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying journey with much promise, consecutive defeats in their last two outings have seen Mauritania's fortunes take a turn for the worse.

Aboubakary Koita, Mamadou Diallo and Alverca striker Dawda Camara all hit the target to fire Les Mourabitounes to a 3-1 opening-day victory over Central African Republic on September 24, five days before crashing back to earth in a 2-1 loss against Benin.

Aritz Lopez Garai’s side were left red-faced on their return to the qualifiers at the weekend, when they fell to a 1-0 defeat against Burkina Faso in the first of their November double-header at the Stade du 4 Aout, with Moise Kabore netting the winner in the 91st minute to sink the visitors.

Having missed the 2025 AFCON, Mauritania find themselves under pressure for a result heading into Tuesday as they sit third in the Group F standings, behind Benin and Burkina Faso, who sit tied on seven points in the first two places.

As for Burkina Faso, head coach Amir Abdou will be pleased with his side’s display on Friday, particularly as it represents a positive response to their crushing 7-0 friendly defeat at the hands of three-time World Champions Argentina in their previous outing on October 4.

The Stallions are now closing on a third straight competitive victory since October 2024, after kicking off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 1-1 stalemate against Benin in Ouagadougou on September 25, three days before securing a 1-0 win over Central African Republic thanks to a 60th-minute strike from Salzburg striker Aboubacar Camara.

Burkina Faso, who sit 62nd in the latest FIFA World Rankings, are aiming to secure a fourth consecutive AFCON appearance, having finished fourth in 2021 before consecutive round-of-16 exits in 2023 and 2025 respectively.

Abdou’s men will be backing themselves to take pole position in Group F on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have failed to win 10 of the previous 12 meetings between the two nations, losing seven and claiming three draws since May 1987.

JS Kabylie defender Aly Abeid was forced off injured midway through the game against Burkina Faso at the weekend, and the 28-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday's tie.

In his absence, Olympique Akbou full-back Khadim Diaw should come into the fold, forming the back four with Ibrahima Keita, Mohamed Ali Diadie and Angers’ man Jordan Lefort.

At the attacking end of the pitch, we expect to see an unchanged front three of Abdoullah Ba, Djeidi Gassama and 26-year-old striker Ndiaga Yade, with ZED FC midfielder Maata Magassa retaining his role at the centre of the park.

Off the back of another solid defensive display, we expect Burkina Faso to name an unchanged back four on Tuesday, with Mamoutou Ouedraogo, Nasser Djiga, Edmond Tapsoba and Arsene Kouassi shielding skipper Herve Koffi between the sticks.

Kabore turned in an eye-catching display to hand the Stallions all three points against Mauritania last time out, and the teenage striker could be rewarded with a starting role here, with Lassina Traore, who has failed to find the back of the net in nine games for club and country since September, swearing over his role in the XI.

Mauritania possible starting lineup:.

Diop; Keita, Diadie, Lefort, Diaw; Magassa, Bodda, Gassama; Ba, Koita, Yade.

Burkina Faso possible starting lineup:.

Koffi; Ouedraogo, Djiga, Tapsoba, Kouassi; Banse, Ouedraogo; Ouattara, Bouda, Zagre; Kabore.

While Mauritania have shown flashes of brilliance in the qualifiers, they find themselves on the cusp of a damaging third consecutive defeat and will be keen to rise to the occasion on Tuesday.

However, Burkina Faso boast superior quality and experience in their rank — particularly at the defensive end of the pitch — and we expect the difference in individual quality to be a decisive factor here, with the Stallions claiming another narrow victory.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

According to recent reports, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

Industry observers note that the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

According to recent reports, “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman noted. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

Industry observers note that “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

It has been revealed that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

In a recent development, it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an matter for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Industry observers note that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

Sources indicate that england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

According to recent reports, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman mentioned. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

According to recent reports, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

In a recent development, all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

According to recent reports, toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Sources indicate that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

Two years after winning their League C group to return to the second tier, Northern Ireland go into Tuesday’s match away to Hungary knowing they will be elevated to League A if they avoid defeat in Budapest.

The turnaround in Northern Ireland’s fortunes in this competition have been stark – prior to coming back up from League C they had just one win in 16 Nations League matches – but this young squad have taken huge steps forward since then.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Asked if he could have predicted Northern Ireland would be in this position with one game left, Barnsley midfielder Kelly told the Press Association: “I wouldn’t say I expected it but I wouldn’t have been shocked.

“I know we have a really good group and we fancy ourselves up against anyone and thankfully results have kind of gone our way and we’ve put ourselves in a really good position.”.

The prospect of moving to the top tier of European football is a huge prize to put in front of this young side.

According to recent reports, the 22-year-old Kelly’s most memorable moment in international football to date came with his fine goal in a 3-1 friendly defeat by France in June. Competitive fixtures against nations of that calibre would be the norm in League A.

Recent findings suggest that “I think that’s a big incentive,” Kelly noted. “It’ll just put us in a really good place if we can top the group, that’ll be a really strong finish to the campaign.

“Playing against teams like France, England, Spain, that would be good to test yourself at that level, to play against them more often and kind of see where we are.”.

Northern Ireland will have to deal with two key suspensions in Budapest, with manager Michael O’Neill needing to watch from the sidelines after picking up a touchline ban, while striker Jamie Donley – who has travelled to Hungary – is also out after getting his second booking.

Kelly noted he was not worried about O’Neill’s ban.

It has been revealed that “Not much changes,” he said. “We’ll just have our game plan ready and go in and try to produce that,” he said. “We’ll just be ready to play the game.”.

Donley’s suspension could offer a bigger role to Kelly with O’Neill weighing how to rejig his attacking options without the man who has led the line throughout this campaign.

“We’ve been working on it now,” Kelly said. “We’re not 100 per cent sure who is going to do that yet. Jamie will be a big miss for us but we’ve got a good squad and whoever’s called upon will be able to go in there and try to replicate what he’s been doing really well for us.”.

Man City: Why the international break could be vital for Maresca

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 06:59.
  • According to recent reports, manchester City began the season with the impression that adapting to Enzo Maresca’s work would be quick.
  • Defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest dropped the team to third place and allowed the current champions to pull clear at the top.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 06:59.

According to recent reports, manchester City began the season with the impression that adapting to Enzo Maresca’s work would be quick. With seven wins in the opening Premier League rounds, the team took the lead and at one point opened up a six-point advantage over Arsenal. The run, however, was abruptly interrupted.

Defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest dropped the team to third place and allowed the current champions to pull clear at the top.

More than the scorelines, the performances exposed difficulties in competing physically, winning duels and protecting the defence when possession is lost. Maresca himself acknowledged that his team could not keep up with the intensity of the opposition in the first half.

It has been revealed that so the November international break comes at a good time. The pause will not erase the problems that have appeared in recent weeks, nor does it mean that all the players will have days off. But it offers the manager a valuable opportunity to assess performance, recover players and work on adjustments that would hardly be possible with a run of matches.

The drop in City’s level cannot be explained only by a lack of efficiency in front of goal.

Sources indicate that the team can still control possession and produce offensive volume. Against Forest, for example, it finished the game with 79 per cent possession and 12 shots. The problem is that this control has not been enough to stop opponents finding space and creating dangerous situations.

According to recent reports, one of the main issues is defensive protection. City have conceded 17 goals in eight matches and have not kept a clean sheet in any of their last nine games. The high defensive line, a hallmark of Maresca’s teams, demands coordination between the units and a quick ability to react to losing the ball. When the counter-press does not work, the defenders are left exposed to fast attacks and have to defend large spaces.

The absence of Rodri helps to explain part of this difficulty. The Spaniard offered reading of the game, interceptions and the quality to organise the build-up. More than a defensive midfielder who protects the defence, he is a player capable of anticipating danger and stopping counter-attacks before they gather speed. Without him, the rest of the midfield has to share responsibilities that Rodri used to take on almost alone.

Elliot Anderson has been important in this context, but so too is the distribution of roles. The presence of players such as Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki adds technical quality and creativity, but also demands defensive cover. If the two play together without a structure that protects the central area, Anderson can be overburdened in covering and in physical duels.

Industry observers note that the break allows Maresca to work on these relationships. One possibility is to adjust the make-up of the midfield, ensuring more balance between creation and protection. Another is to review the team’s positioning without the ball, especially the distance between the defensive line and the most advanced players. It is not necessarily a question of abandoning the style of play, but of finding ways to make it less vulnerable.

The calendar and the physical condition of the squad are another vital aspect. City lost rhythm during a demanding period of fixtures, and the recovery of players can help the team regain the intensity needed to execute Maresca’s model.

Sources indicate that it will also be crucial to monitor the situation of Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. Both were substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because of physical problems, according to Maresca. The break could be useful to assess the extent of the concerns and avoid important players returning before they are fully fit.

In a recent development, there is, however, a caveat: the international break is not a holiday for the whole squad. Several starters have been called up by their national teams, among them Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Gvardiol, Guehi, Enzo Fernandez and Cherki. Travel and international commitments reduce the recovery time for some players, while others will be able to stay in Manchester and work directly with the coaching staff.

Recent findings suggest that even so, the break offers an opportunity to reorganise the workload and prepare the squad for what follows. In a season in which intensity is essential to the functioning of Maresca’s system, managing physical wear and tear is also part of the recovery process.

The break arrives at a time when City need to recover not only results, but also confidence in their own way of playing. The seven opening wins showed that the team has the resources to compete for the title. The three defeats that followed, on the other hand, revealed that there are still key adjustments to be made to sustain that level over an entire season.

It has been revealed that the first challenge after the break will be against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. Then the team will face an even more significant fixture: the visit to Arsenal on 29 November. The six-point gap makes the direct meeting an vital opportunity to close the distance, although the result will not be enough, by itself, to settle the title race.

Industry observers note that for Maresca, the international break is a chance to find answers before the run of negative results turns into an even bigger problem. The manager needs to restore defensive solidity, find the best distribution of roles in midfield and make possession dominance translate into effective control of matches again.

City do not need to abandon their identity to react. Above all, they need to find a better balance between what they do with the ball and what they can do when they lose it. If the break allows Maresca to progress with this work and recover crucial players, the team could return better prepared to face a decisive stretch of the season.

AC Milan are, once again, left looking at a disappointing performance from Goncalo Ramos; this time it was for Portugal.

It has been revealed that it’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been unsatisfactory. The Portuguese started brightly in his first two games, but has since struggled to really hit the highs expected of him after an almost €90 million deal was agreed in the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With another international break, the hope was that he’d rediscover the form from the last set of games and bring it back to San Siro, but it hasn’t happened that way yet.

Speaking in the mixed zone after Portugal’s heavy defeat, Ramos looked at what went wrong in the game and what needs to be corrected next time, as MilanPress relays.

“I think it was a tough match. They studied our team well, and even the details ultimately fell in their favour. Then we ended up losing momentum a bit, but that’s something that happens and is part of it.

“We’re first in the most vital group. We already have another match in three days, so it’s not worth dwelling too much on what happened today. There’s already a match ahead, and it’s very important.”.

In a recent development, “In the end, they managed to apply better pressure on us. We weren’t able to find many options, and that ended up hurting our game because we like to have clean, controlled possession of the ball, and that’s what makes the difference in our game.

“On the one hand, it’s good to have a match in three days and not have to spend three or four months thinking about a defeat like that. We already have a game to respond and to erase what happened here today.

It has been revealed that “The conversation in the locker room after the game was that we’re first and we have a game to clean up after what happened today. That’s the goal of the team and the group.”.

Considering he’s now the out-and-out first-choice striker for Portugal, it’s a lot of pressure on his shoulders for club and country. Hopefully he can start to thrive under the pressure, rather than succumbing to it.

There are six play-off places up for grabs this season, therefore the Blades are just two points adrift of a spot in spite of their inconsistency.

Retired stopper Ikeme, who had a brief spell on loan at Bramall Lane from Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2009, does not expect Sheffield United to fade away.

Recent findings suggest that he told The Yorkshire Post: “There's extra play-off positions this year, I think a lot of the clubs will be looking at that. I think Sheffield United will definitely be up and around it, especially with everything they've got. They've got a strong team as well still.

“I don't think they'll go up automatically, I don't think they're stronger than the other teams but I think they'll be around the play-offs in those positions, along with 10-12 teams that’ll be thinking they're going to make the play-offs this year already, and I think Sheffield United will be one of them as well.”.

Opinions may be forming at this stage of the season in a 46-game campaign, there are plenty of twists and turns yet to come.

Ikeme said: “The Championship’s not about now, it's about March, April, and I think teams will hit their run of form and will hit a brick wall at some stage.

“It will be up to them to see if they can get through it and see if they will go up.

“[Sheffield United have] great support, a great stadium, great atmosphere, but obviously Chris Wilder is a really experienced manager and he knows what he's doing.”.

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:01, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 07:11.

Arsenal have been handed an injury scare after Martin Zubimendi was forced off during Spain's defeat to England on Sunday evening.

The Gunners midfielder appeared to suffer a hamstring problem in the second half at the Metropolitano Stadium, prompting Luis de la Fuente to replace him with Nico Williams.

The extent of the problem remains unclear, but his availability for the north Londoners' upcoming fixtures is surely now a concern for manager Mikel Arteta.

Zubimendi's evening took a disappointing turn after he was forced off with an apparent hamstring injury during La Roja's 3-2 defeat to the Three Lions in the UEFA Nations League.

Spain had initially fallen three goals behind following strikes from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White, before attempting to mount a comeback after Elliot Anderson's red card.

However, the £55m Arsenal midfielder was unable to continue, with Athletic Club winger Williams introduced in his place.

The injury will concern Arteta, particularly with Arsenal facing a demanding schedule as the campaign heads towards the festive period.

It remains too early to establish how long Zubimendi could be sidelined, but an extended absence would put his participation in several important fixtures in doubt.

Arsenal are scheduled to face Newcastle United away in the Premier League, Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League and title rivals Manchester City before the end of the month, meaning the 27-year-old could miss a significant run of matches if the injury proves serious.

Any lengthy absence for Zubimendi would be a frustrating development for Arteta, who needs as many of his key players available as possible during an increasingly busy period.

The festive schedule is approaching, with domestic and European commitments leaving little room for the manager to rest his first-choice players.

Although Declan Rice has continued to impress, losing another midfield option would reduce Arteta's flexibility when rotating his squad and managing workloads.

Zubimendi has not always enjoyed the game time he might have expected following his arrival in 2025, but that does not diminish his importance as a squad option.

Arsenal will now hope the injury is relatively minor and that the midfielder can return rapidly, so until the extent of the problem is established, his availability for the upcoming fixtures must remain a concern.

Data experts Opta have deployed a supercomputer to predict how the League Two table will look at the end of the 2026/27 campaign.

International football took a wrecking ball to the EFL fixture calendar over the weekend but there was still plenty of fourth-tier action.

Rotherham United’s meeting with Crawley Town did not go ahead but York City were in action and secured their first away win of the season, defeating Rochdale 1-0.

Minstermen boss Scott Lindsey remarked: “It’s a massive monkey off our back for us to get that first away win. There have been times when we’ve deserved to win away, there haven’t been many where we’ve not played well, we’ve been good away from home. But you do think ‘when is that first away win going to come?’ and it becomes psychological.”.

Away from Yorkshire, Salford City were held to a 1-1 draw by Northampton Town and Shrewsbury Town claimed a 2-1 win over Oldham Athletic. Grimsby Town completed a 4-1 rout of Swindon Town, Fleetwood Town edged past Tranmere Roevrs and Port Vale saw off Accrington Stanley.

Crewe Alexandra drew 2-2 with Newport County and Colchester United got the better of Gillingham, while Bristol Rovers lost to Chesterfield and Exeter City clinched a narrow 1-0 win over Cheltenham Town.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:31.

Manchester United could target Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie as new boss Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen his options at Old Trafford.

The American international has worked under Pochettino with the USMNT, and the Argentine is understood to be a major admirer of his versatility.

However, McKennie's previous spell in English football raises questions over whether he would represent the right addition for United in January.

According to reports in Italy, Pochettino could attempt to reunite with McKennie once he officially takes the reins at United.

The outgoing United States head coach has previously spoken highly of the Juventus midfielder, once describing him as the equivalent of 'McKennie plus 10' when discussing his importance to the team.

McKennie has also impressed at club level, becoming an key figure under Luciano Spalletti and making 241 appearances for Juventus.

The 28-year-old recently signed a contract extension until 2030, meaning Juventus are in a strong negotiating position and would reportedly demand a substantial offer before considering his departure.

However, the Italian club are not ruling out potential sales as they look to reshape their squad and remain within UEFA's financial regulations.

McKennie's tactical flexibility is understood to appeal to Pochettino, with the USMNT star capable of operating in several midfield roles and further forward.

A January move is therefore a possibility worth monitoring, particularly given United's need to strengthen their options in the middle of the park.

There are reasons to question whether McKennie would be the right signing for United, though, given his previous experience in the Premier League.

His loan spell at Leeds United in 2023 was largely disappointing, with the 28-year-old midfielder unable to make the desired impact as the club suffered relegation.

He made 19 appearances, collecting seven bookings, while struggling to adapt to the demands of English football and facing criticism over his fitness and discipline.

Although Leeds' wider problems contributed to their disappointing campaign, McKennie did little to establish himself as a standout performer.

His versatility and familiarity with Pochettino could make him useful, but United should arguably be targeting a higher calibre of midfielder if they want to address their long-standing problems.

With significant investment needed elsewhere in the squad, spending heavily on a player who has already struggled in England would represent a considerable gamble.

Former Leeds United goalkeeper Paul Robinson does not believe there is “any need” for Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel to immediately replace Jordan Pickford with James Trafford.

Game time has been evenly split between Everton’s Pickford and Leeds’ Trafford across the last two international breaks, with the latter pushing to dislodge the former.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Trafford has made a stellar start to life at Leeds since his summer switch from Manchester City and shone in England’s 3-2 Nations League win over Spain at the weekend.

The 24-year-old has been showered with praise but Robinson, who also represented England in his playing days, has preached patience.

According to recent reports, writing for The i, he remarked: “At the moment, I don’t see there’s any need to replace Jordan. Without a doubt, the next major tournament he will be playing, but he’ll be 34.

It has been revealed that “It just goes to show Tuchel sees this as a long-term project. He’s not in overnight thinking, how do I win the next game? He’s preparing for life further down the road – and life after Jordan Pickford.”.

Robinson may not be advocating for an immediate change between the sticks, yet is a strong admirer of Leeds’ club-record signing.

He has suggested Trafford - who cost the Whites a hefty £40m - has the potential to enter the elite goalkeeper bracket.

The 47-year-old said: “As English goalkeepers, we haven’t had one quite in the bracket of Ederson, Alisson, Thibaut Courtois at their peaks. The bracket underneath, we’re flush with.

“Trafford has the potential to enter that top bracket, while Pickford has improved as a person and a player. There was a lot of talk about his antics on the pitch – he’s understood who he is, and he’s channelled the best part of him in the right way.”.

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:53, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 07:53.

Liverpool and Chelsea are among three Premier League clubs monitoring AC Milan defender Koni De Winter ahead of the January transfer window.

The 24-year-old has impressed at the San Siro this season, attracting attention alongside Manchester United.

However, the Serie A giants are reluctant to sanction his departure and consider him an notable part of their long-term defensive intends.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Liverpool, Chelsea and United have all 'shown interest' in De Winter after his impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign.

The Belgium international joined Milan from Genoa in the summer of 2025 and made 26 appearances in his debut season, gradually establishing himself as a reliable defensive option.

He has taken another step forward this term, featuring 11 times in Serie A and becoming an crucial member of the backline under ex-Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

De Winter's versatility is particularly attractive, having demonstrated an ability to operate in both a back three and a conventional back four.

His physical attributes and composure in possession have also helped him develop into an increasingly complete defender, with Milan viewing the £20m-rated titan as a potential future leader.

The Rossoneri are keen to strengthen their own defence in January, with Sporting CP's Goncalo Inacio reportedly a major target, but that does not necessarily mean De Winter will be allowed to leave.

Liverpool and Chelsea could find themselves competing for several of the same players in January, with both clubs looking to strengthen their defensive options and improve the overall balance of their squads.

Their joint interest in AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is another example, with both Premier League sides having been linked with a £100m move for the highly-rated Englishman.

De Winter would offer a different type of opportunity, potentially providing either club with a versatile defensive option capable of covering multiple positions.

There are clear similarities between the recruitment needs of the Reds and the Blues, meaning their paths could cross repeatedly as the winter window approaches.

However, Milan's determination to retain De Winter means a deal will not be straightforward, particularly if they are unwilling to entertain anything short of a substantial offer.

With Scott and De Winter both on their respective radars, the two English clubs could be set for an intriguing January transfer battle.

Minimalist biotechnology companies that have just a handful of employees — or even as few as one — are becoming more feasible with the rise of artificial-intelligence tools.Credit: Getty.

How many scientists does it take to discover a drug?

The question came to the fore after news that a biotechnology company armed with an artificial-intelligence assistant, two promising drug leads and just one full-time human employee had been acquired by San Francisco-based Anthropic as part of the AI giant’s expansion into biomedical science.

AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more.

AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, it took many human scientists to develop the molecules that are the mini-company’s star products: two antibodies that are still in the early stages of development and were designed to treat a rare form of muscular dystrophy. The company, Mithril Medicine in Cambridge, Massachusetts, also hired part-time consultants to advise on the project, and paid at least five contract research organizations to conduct experiments. Many more researchers will be needed to carry the drug further, especially if it eventually enters clinical trials. “It takes a village to develop a drug,” states Jeb Keiper, a partner at Third Rock Ventures, a venture-capital firm in Boston, Massachusetts.

Industry observers note that but the news sparked a wave of discussions about whether the one-person biotech is the drug-discovery business model of the future. “We will see more and more of these small teams that are enabled by AI,” indicates James Zou, a computer scientist who works on biomedical applications of AI at Stanford University in California. “They will be very powerful for identifying good opportunities and moving promptly.”.

Industry observers note that itsy-bitsy biotechs are not a newly introduced concept. Entrepreneur Matt Davidson started his first biotech tech giant in 2013, nearly a decade before ChatGPT’s public debut. Davidson kept the roster trim for years, with only two full-time employees until the drug he was developing was ready to enter late-stage clinical testing. The company never had a physical laboratory, Davidson says. All the lab work was contracted out.

His current manufacturer, Azora Therapeutics in Los Angeles, California, has a whopping five employees. He uses AI more for summarizing reports than for scientific discovery and notes that AI tools have made tiny biotechs more efficient. “We use consultants a little bit less than we used to,” he says.

Industry observers note that anthropic’s AI biolab finds ‘CRISPR-like’ DNA in viruses. What’s next?

Anthropic’s AI biolab finds ‘CRISPR-like’ DNA in viruses. What’s next?

Mithril Medicine leaned more heavily on AI than Azora does, and tasked Anthropic’s AI assistant Claude with helping to analyse data and suggesting next steps, as well as taming the piles of e-mails and paperwork that come from working with multiple contract research organizations. “What began as an exercise in staying lean evolved into the thesis for an entirely new operating model, which we now call Pipeline-in-a-Person,” wrote Cody Tranbarger, Mithril’s former chief executive and lone employee, on LinkedIn. (Tranbarger, who has worked for Anthropic since Mithril was absorbed into it, declined to speak to Nature, as did Anthropic.).

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 09:32, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 09:38.

England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run in all competitions courtesy of a 3-2 success in Madrid in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday night.

An extraordinary match saw England lead 3-0 before Spain attempted to launch a fightback, but the Three Lions held on to secure all three points.

The result has allowed England to top Group 3 of League A in the Nations League.

Spain have joined Thomas Tuchel's side in the quarter-finals of the tournament, but their long unbeaten run has now come to an end.

Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi was handed another start in the middle of the Spain midfield, but it proved to be a difficult night for the 27-year-old, who played in a protective mark due to a broken nose that he suffered while playing for the Gunners last month.

Zubimendi was substituted in the 72nd minute due to an apparent injury, and it remains to be seen whether he is now facing a period on the sidelines.

El Desmarque were especially critical of Zubimendi, saying that the midfielder was simply "overwhelmed" by England, who adopted a high-press from the very first whistle.

AS also detailed Zubimendi's problems, with the publication noting his struggles to dictate the play against Gunners teammate Declan Rice, while his use of the ball was also criticised.

Mundo Deportivo stated that the midfielder was "exhausted" due to England's press, with Zubimendi hardly ever given time to settle on the ball.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult start to the season for Zubimendi, and there has recently been speculation surrounding his future.

The midfielder has played 12 times for the Gunners this term, but he has not made a single start in the Premier League, with his seven outings - totalling 101 minutes - coming from the bench, while he has played just 98 minutes of Champions League football this term.

Zubimendi is not at the moment first choice in the Arsenal midfield, and his lack of football this season could have contributed to his struggles against England, as the 27-year-old did appear to lack sharpness in the Nations League fixture.

It remains to be seen whether the Spaniard stays at Arsenal on a long-term basis, but it is believed that a number of La Liga clubs are keen to bring him back to the division next year.

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 09:42.

Leeds United and Newcastle United have reportedly identified Coventry City midfielder Jack Rudoni as a potential transfer target.

The playmaker started 2026-27 having never played Premier League football, instead representing the likes of AFC Wimbledon and Huddersfield Town prior to his transfer to the CBS Arena in 2024.

However, the 24-year-old has quickly progressed into one of the Sky Blues' key players in their first top-flight campaign for 25 years.

Rudoni has netted three goals in 10 appearances, including efforts in wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland.

According to Football Insider, clubs higher up the Premier League table have started to take an interest in his signature.

The report claims that Leeds and Newcastle are among several clubs who are monitoring any developments with Rudoni's future.

With a contract until 2028, Coventry's position at the negotiating table is weakening when it comes to retaining Rudoni in their squad.

An agreement over fresh terms is realistically unlikely to be found until it is determined whether Coventry will retain their Premier League status for 2027-28.

That noted, Coventry allegedly have no interest in considering any offers for Rudoni during the winter transfer window.

From Newcastle's perspective, it is suggested that Rudoni is viewed as an alternative to the likes of Joe Willock and Joelinton, who may both leave the Magpies next year.

If Rudoni continues along his current trajectory, interest and offers will continue to arrive, and he will have the chance of making a more lucrative move to a bigger club.

A total of 21 goals and 21 assists have been contributed from 94 appearances in a Coventry shirt.

Coventry paid in the region of £5m when they signed Rudoni in 2024, and failing to agree a fresh contract will naturally leave them in a position where they will have to consider cashing in for a substantial profit.

Given his homegrown status, he will be viewed as an asset to any Premier League club outside of the established top teams in the division.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

According to recent reports, the three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a joy to watch,” Arteta remarked. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. According to recent reports, arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his upcoming Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

In a recent development, lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 09:47, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 09:48.

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA leadership as he believes that president Gianni Infantino is worse than disgraced predecessor Sepp Blatter.

Infantino has spent the last 10 years in the most powerful position in global football and has frequently faced criticism, but widespread backlash aimed at the 56-year-old Swiss chief has grown since the 2026 World Cup.

In the summer, Infantino came under fire for his involvement in overturning a red card suspension for USA striker Folarin Balogun following a phone call from U.S. President Donald Trump.

Infantino's position at FIFA was plunged into a deeper crisis when he unveiled controversial prepares to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

This attracted major opposition from several football confederations including UEFA, who threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments, but the ‘FIFA Forward Enterprises’ has since been scrapped.

Infantino became FIFA president in 2016 after former chief Blatter stepped down amid a ​major corruption scandal that lead to him facing criminal charges.

Infantino was then re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023, and intends to stand again for a fourth term in March, but Klopp is one high-profile figure keen for change at the very top of football.

Indeed, the Germany boss made his feelings clear on Infantino during a press conference ahead of Germany’s UEFA Nations League showdown with the Netherlands on Monday.

“The general consensus is that a change might make sense,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters.

“After Sepp Blatter, we thought things couldn’t get any worse, and then we managed to pull it off.

“There are certainly people who care about football and have no financial interests. If one of them were to take over, it would be absolutely helpful.”.

While working as a pundit before taking the Germany job earlier this year, Klopp slammed the decision for Balogun’s red card to be overturned at the World Cup, and was particularly critical of Trump’s apparent involvement.

“If that really was the case, then that’s crazy,” Klopp noted in July. “Let’s just say: this is our game, not theirs.

It has been revealed that “These two people (Trump and Infantino), who both have no idea about football, should have nothing to do with that. That was a red card. There’s no two ways about it.”.

Klopp was appointed Germany head coach a few weeks later, replacing Julian Nagelsmann following the country’s shock last-32 exit on penalties to Paraguay at the World Cup.

The 59-year-old has not publicly stated who he would like to see take the FIFA presidency from Infantino, but former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega and Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima have unveiled their intention to challenge him.

Meanwhile, former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Infantino as a candidate in FIFA’s presidential election, despite allegedly receiving backing from France president Emmanuel Macron.

Wenger - who had distanced himself from Infantino’s aborted FIFA Forward Enterprises blueprint - currently holds the role of Head of Global Development at FIFA and is expected to continue in this position.

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

In a recent development, 'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss.

In a recent development, 'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

It has been revealed that 'Declan Rice remarked he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'.

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

Industry observers note that 'The red card and the penalty is always a substantial decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'.

Everton and Nottingham Forest are reportedly ready to do battle for Gremio defender Gustavo Martins.

The Toffees and Tricky Trees right now sit in sixth and 16th position in the Premier League table.

However, David Moyes and Oliver Glasner will be encouraged by the defensive numbers that their teams are producing.

While Forest have conceded just 13 goals in 10 games, Everton have the joint-fourth best record in the division having only shipped 10 goals.

Nevertheless, as per Fussball Europa, Martins has emerged as a potential transfer target for both clubs.

The 24-year-old has netted 13 times from his 129 appearances for the Brazilian club.

He is predominantly a centre-back, but his versatility has been shown with outings at right-back, too.

Twenty-one of his 24 appearances for Gremio this season have come from the starting lineup. Gremio at the moment sit in 18th position in the Brasileiro table.

If Gremio are relegated to the second tier, they are likely to be inundated with offers for a player in Martins whose contract is due to expire in December 2027.

Regardless, Gremio have allegedly already set an asking price in the region of €12m (£10.02m) to €15m (£12.52m).

With a strong Brazilian contingent at Forest, there are clear reasons as to why Martins may be interested in signing for Forest.

However, they already have four senior centre-back options who have long-term contracts in place at the City Ground.

In sharp contrast, two of Everton's top three central defenders - James Tarkowski and Michael Keane - are 33 years of age, while Moyes is generally short of strength-in-depth.

Therefore, Martins moving to the Hill Dickinson Stadium would make far more sense if he wants to earn regular opportunities should he choose to move to England.

#14212. Tech Report: Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

Tech Report: Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the Francis Crick Institute in London celebrates its tenth anniversary and I look back on my first year as chief executive, I find myself reflecting on both how much has been achieved and how profoundly life science is changing.
  • Industry observers note that as an epigeneticist, I can safely say that history and context matter.
  • The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the Francis Crick Institute in London celebrates its tenth anniversary and I look back on my first year as chief executive, I find myself reflecting on both how much has been achieved and how profoundly life science is changing.

Industry observers note that as an epigeneticist, I can safely say that history and context matter. When I began my scientific career in the 1980s, experiments were painstaking, time-consuming, expensive and repetitive. Generating a knockout mouse or sequencing a gene could take weeks or months, and required resources that were available at few institutions.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an enhancement.

Biology has since entered an extraordinary era. It is increasingly multidisciplinary, and researchers have an unprecedented range of technologies at their disposal, from single-cell and spatial biology techniques to advanced imaging, genome editing, tissue engineering and computational approaches.

Artificial intelligence is also transforming science. Its ability to bring together complex data sets offers fresh ways to connect the study of biology across scales, from molecules and cells to individual organisms and populations. It is also enabling the democratization of discovery and knowledge. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold system, for example, has made predictions of millions of protein structures available to researchers worldwide.

Industry observers note that biologists are poised to at last understand the complexity of life: the influence of the environment, ageing and sex, alongside genetics, on the differences between us. Among the questions to which answers are within reach are how the genetic code gives rise to a living organism; how the control and expression of genes varies during development; how tissues communicate and bodily functions depend on one another; and why diseases develop differently in different people and treatments work for some but not others.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Reductionism has served biology well, giving us a deep mechanistic understanding of life, health and disease. But many features of living systems cannot be predicted from their individual parts alone. They emerge from interactions between components and depend on the context in which those interactions occur.

Science needs both reductionist and holistic approaches: connecting molecular mechanisms and signalling pathways with inter-organ communication and physiology, while understanding how these systems respond and adapt to environmental challenges. And performing such studies requires research environments that allow scientists to think and work across conventional boundaries.

Recent findings suggest that as director of the Crick, I have seen the incredible value of an environment that is organized around people and scientific questions rather than institutional divisions. Shared infrastructure and specialist teams enable research to cross disciplines and deploy technologies in new ways. Connections between fundamental research, clinical science and industry also help discoveries to move towards real-world applications, swiftly and efficiently.

It has been revealed that but even the most sophisticated technologies and research environments are only as powerful as the scientists using them. Creating an environment in which people from diverse backgrounds and with different life experiences are encouraged to perform bold, rigorous science and harness the power of AI will be key to future discoveries. Patterns identified by AI need to be scrutinized by people and validated through experiment.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03669-w.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea failed with an approach to sign Real Betis winger Jose Antonio Morante, according to reports in Spain.

The 19-year-old made his first-team breakthrough with Real Betis earlier this year and has made three appearances for the Spanish club this season.

In a recent development, in the summer, Morante was a key part of the Spain squad which won the UEFA European Under-19 Championship. He finished in the Team of the Tournament with five of his Spain teammates and ended the tournament as the joint-top scorer with four goals.

According to ABC Sevilla, Chelsea monitored Morante during the European Under-19 Championship and made an approach to the winger’s representatives in the summer transfer window.

However, Morante is understood to have personally turned down a move to Chelsea as he wants to become a first-team regular with his boyhood club Real Betis.

ABC Sevilla add that Chelsea have been ‘persistent’ with their interest but Morante has made it clear that he wants to stay with the Spanish club.

In July, Morante signed a new deal with Real Betis which keeps him tied to the club until 2030 and includes a €30 million (£25m) release clause.

Bayern Munich are thinking about life after Manuel Neuer and are looking for a long-term successor to their historic goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that the 40-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season. The Bavarian club have explored several options, with two Ligue 1 goalkeepers on their shortlist: Kevin Trapp (Paris FC) and Lukas Hradecky (Monaco).

A third name can now be added: Robin Risser. According to information from Gianluca Di Marzio, Bayern Munich are taking a close interest in Risser’s profile. The Bavarian club have even made first contact and blueprint to step up their efforts soon.

The German giants already have a strategy in mind to sign the Lens goalkeeper.

The Italian journalist says Bayern intend to sign the 21-year-old in the January transfer window, then loan him back to Lens for the second half of the season, before being able to count on him from next season. For the moment, no fee has emerged for this approach.

The advantage of this recruitment strategy is that it allows Risser to continue to progress at the northern club until the end of this season.

However, Bayern Munich are not alone in the race, as five other European heavyweights are interested: Manchester City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Inter Milan and Juventus. Lens are reportedly demanding at least £34m (€40m).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United plan to make a move for Como star Nico Paz as early as the January transfer window and make him one of Mauricio Pochettino’s first signings at Old Trafford.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half year deal in Manchester with hope he can lift the club after their worst start to a season in 40 years.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be backed in the January window with up front and left-back believed to be two areas that could be strengthened.

With Bruno Fernandes’ long-term future in doubt, United are also monitoring Argentina international Paz.

The 22-year-old tormented Michael Carrick’s side in the Champions League last month, scoring twice and providing an assist in a 4-1 victory having grown into one of Serie A’s brightest talents under Cesc Fabregas.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid with Los Blancos retaining a £67million buy-back clause which can be activated next summer.

While recent reports have suggested United’s interest in Paz is with a summer move in mind, Argentine newspaper Clarin now claims they could bring plans forward, with the attacking midfielder now on their shortlist of January targets.

Aware of Real’s summer buy-back clause, the report states United could accelerate negotiations and use Pochettino’s arrival to convince him to make the move to Manchester in early 2027, beating Real to the punch.

Real explored the possibility of re-signing Paz last summer with the player telling Jose Mourinho he wished to stay in Italy to continue his development.

Jurgen Klopp has hailed Kai Havertz as a “complete” player, as he explained why he shares Mikel Arteta’s trust in the Arsenal striker.

Havertz led the line for Germany in their 3-1 win over Serbia on Saturday, returning straight to his country’s starting lineup after injury.

He started Klopp’s first match in charge of the national team against the Netherlands in September but then missed the next three games during that break due to a hamstring problem.

Despite having limited opportunities to work with Havertz in the early stages of his Germany reign, Klopp has made it clear just how highly he rates the 27-year-old.

“I’ve played against Kai many times, and I can tell you that preparing for a game against him is no walk in the park,” Klopp said.

According to recent reports, “You get a real sense of just how complete a player he is. You always have to be prepared for him to produce an outstanding performance because he has all the qualities to do so. He’s a top player.

“Mikel Arteta is someone who, as a person and as a coach, is absolutely determined to win. And unless several negative scenarios all come together, Kai Havertz starts games for Arsenal.

“The fact that he plays here is not simply because I don’t want to leave him out, but because I want to win games.”.

Havertz started the season in superb form for Arsenal, scoring in wins over Coventry and Chelsea in the opening weeks of the campaign.

His performances have dipped in recent weeks since the hamstring matter, though Arteta has insisted that injury is not still impacting Havertz.

Recent findings suggest that the criticism of Havertz in the last chunk of matches for Arsenal has been his finishing. Particularly in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood, Havertz was extremely wasteful.

Manchester United reportedly have no plans to allow Noussair Mazraoui to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

There is currently speculation surrounding the Morocco international's future, with AC Milan and Juventus both believed to be keeping a close eye on the defender's situation.

Various clubs in Saudi Arabia are also thought to be interested in the 28-year-old.

However, according to the Daily Briefing, the 20-time English champions are not interested in selling the versatile defender in the middle of the campaign.

Mazraoui made the move to Man United from Bayern Munich in 2024, and he has made 85 appearances for the 20-time English champions.

The full-back has featured on eight occasions for the Red Devils this season, providing one assist, and he played the full 90 minutes of the team's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League before the international break.

It remains to be seen how heavily Mazraoui features under upcoming Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, who will officially begin work at Old Trafford on Thursday.

Mazraoui is right now with the Morocco squad in this international period, helping his national team to record a 5-1 win over Niger on November 13.

The defender is also due to be involved in the second clash with Niger on November 17 before heading back to Man United to prepare for Sunday's Premier League game against Liverpool.

Incoming Man United head coach Pochettino has big decisions to make when it comes to his back four for Sunday's Premier League game against Liverpool.

Luke Shaw could be available again after a period on the sidelines, while Lisandro Martinez is also free to return to the squad, having served a suspension against Villa.

Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu are also options at the back, and it will be fascinating to see which defensive unit is selected by Pochettino this weekend.

Should Shaw again be ruled out, Mazraoui would have a strong chance of being named in the starting team at Anfield.
