Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Manchester City’s players have not mentioned much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, claims he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

According to recent reports, ‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

Industry observers note that ‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’.

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

Industry observers note that ‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

In a recent development, ‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a newly introduced nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that notes everything.’.

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

It has been revealed that ‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I noted, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

Sources indicate that ‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’.

Argentine boss Pochettino will finish his stint off as head coach of the United States men’s national team with the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals, welcoming Haiti Stateside with a 6-0 aggregate lead in the early hours of Wednesday.

Pochettino will then cross the pond to start life as Manchester United manager, ahead of his first game in charge of the Red Devils against arch-rivals Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

US Soccer have until March to appoint Pochettino’s replacement, with their next head coach’s first games likely to be the semi-finals of the Nations League.

Former Manchester City boss Guardiola was linked with the role, but after reports he is set to reject any approach from US Soccer, the ex-Barcelona manager has drifted to third with the bookies, at odds of 5/1.

Sources indicate that despite all the star coaches being mentioned with the vacancy, the current frontrunners are two Americans. Nashville SC head coach BJ Callaghan is the favourite at the time of writing, given odds of 3/1.

His fellow countryman Steve Cherundolo, right now in charge of the USA’s Under-23 squad, is second-favourite, priced at 4/1.

Recent findings suggest that arguably the most recognisable American name in world football at the moment, Jesse Marsch has rather long odds of 30/1. This is explained by his current employment as manager of neighbours Canada, and a history of negative comments towards the USSF.

According to recent reports, pellegrino Matarazzo is another American coach, presently working in Spain as head coach of Real Sociedad in La Liga. Having impressed enough to be given a latest two-year deal ahead of this season, Matarazzo is priced at 6/1, reflecting the difficulty of both matching the required compensation and convincing the head coach to leave a job managing in the Europa League.

A host of out of work managers have also been linked to the vacancy. Former England boss Gareth Southgate and ex-Germany head coach Julian Naglesmann have been priced at 25/1, some distance from Thierry Henry and Roberton Martinez - who both sit on odds of 14/1.

With Mauricio Pochettino expected on the bench at Manchester United, Marcus Rashford is already being presented as the potential substantial winner of the appointment. It is also surely the last chance for the England international at a major European club.

Following the sacking of Michael Carrick, Pochettino will succeed him and is expected at Manchester United on a surprising date: Wednesday 18 November, late in the day, less than four days before the Premier League clash at Liverpool on 22 November. It is a late arrival, as the current United States head coach will end his time in charge of that team overnight on Tuesday into Wednesday (midnight UK time) against Haiti.

Either way, Pochettino’s expected appointment is already making plenty of noise. While people wonder what style of play to expect from the Argentine manager, who is more of a 4-2-3-1 follower, a first winner of his arrival is being mentioned.

The Telegraph reports that ‘Rashford is tipped to be the substantial winner of Pochettino’s appointment’.

According to the outlet, the former Tottenham boss has always been a fan of the England winger.

Industry observers note that he notably wanted to sign him while in charge of PSG. ‘Mauricio has always loved Rashford. He will put an arm around him and give him the same kind of love he demonstrated Dele Alli [at Tottenham]. Then it will be up to Rashford,’ - sources close to the 54-year-old noted.

According to recent reports, pochettino should therefore take the 29-year-old, who has been out with a hip injury for almost a month, under his wing. The date of his return is not yet known. In any case, the Argentine’s arrival comes at the right time for Rashford, who is going through a difficult spell at United.

ssful loan at Barcelona last season, the England international is struggling at Old Trafford.

If he does not relaunch his career under Pochettino, those doors are unlikely to reopen.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

According to recent reports, owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness remarked on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

In a recent development, ‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Industry observers note that he plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

‘He isn’t the complete midfield player.’.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice mentioned: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Declan Rice hit TWO worldie free-kicks vs Real Madrid 🤯So nice he did it twice ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zg5CzlQQNh.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

According to recent reports, ‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Ravenna's club executives have left the door open for Ronaldinho to play for the Serie C side again after his remarkable comeback to professional football.

Ronaldinho appeared in his first match since 2015 on Sunday, playing the opening 45 minutes in Ravenna's 2-0 win over Forli at Stadio Comunale Bruno Benelli.

The 46-year-old joined Ravenna as an investor in August and worked his way up to fitness before making an appearance for the third-tier outfit.

He had been due to play for the first 30 minutes, but instead lasted until half-time before he was replaced by Matteo Maggio.

Ronaldinho was unable to score the 300th goal of his career, but he put in a solid display, completing 17 of his 21 passes while also creating a chance from a corner.

After 14 games of the 2026-27 season, Ravenna sit second in Group B of the Serie C standings, six points adrift of Spice.

But speaking after their win at the weekend, Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani told Sky Italia that Ronaldinho could feature again for the team in the future.

"He didn't want to come off, he was having fun," Cipriani noted.

When asked about a possible return, Cipriani stated: "We'll see how things go.".

A post shared by Ravenna Football Club (@ravennafootballclub).

Cipriani's comments were echoed by Ravenna's vice president Ariedo Braida, who was at AC Milan when Ronaldinho played there between 2008 and 2011.

"A champion like him enchants young and old alike, everyone has fallen in love with Ronaldinho," he said.

"There are those who know how to play football and those who kick a ball. He knows how to play football. I hope to see him here again.".

Ravenna have won their last four league matches, and face eighth-place Livorno this weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he rolled out a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very rapidly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Industry observers note that ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a significant game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

It has been revealed that no one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring challenges to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the manufacturer man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

Recent findings suggest that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

According to recent reports, but domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

In a recent development, atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

In a recent development, simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

Recent findings suggest that the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05.
  • Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has confirmed that he has retired from international football.
  • With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05.

Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has confirmed that he has retired from international football.

With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.

Lukaku's most recent outing for Belgium was against France on November 5, the 33-year-old donning the captain's armband on that occasion.

However, Lukaku did not play in Belgium's last two fixtures, being ruled out versus Turkey last Thursday due to a hip injury and remaining as an unused substitute for Sunday's 4-1 victory over Italy.

On Monday morning, Lukaku took to social media to make the surprise revelation that he had called time on his international career.

A statement on Instagram read: "Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team…I experienced every emotion imaginable….

"I was lucky enough to play alongside extraordinary teammates, to whom I will always be grateful. I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches who pushed me to give my best and trusted me to help the team. It was a wonderful journey, and I cherished every moment.

"To the Belgian fans, thank you for all the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was incredible. I enjoyed it immensely. I am grateful. Thank you.".

Under both Rudi Garcia at the World Cup and Mark van Bommel across the six recent UEFA Nations League matches, Lukaku has not been viewed as a certain starter.

That is despite the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scoring in four of his last seven outings for his country.

While Lukaku has not shed light on any potential problems behind the scenes, an assumption can be made that remaining as an unused substitute in two of the five games that he was available under Van Bommel has played its part.

At the age of 33, Lukaku had the opportunity to join a list of players who have reached 100 goals for their country. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Ali Daei have achieved that feat.

Choosing to stay six goals short of the illustrious three figures feels an unusual choice on Lukaku's part, but it does not take away from ending his international career with 53 goals more than any other Belgian player in history.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino is set to begin work with Manchester United imminently, with his backroom staff already in the UK.

The Argentine’s assistants, Jesus Perez, Toni Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), all of whom worked with him in the United States setup, flew to England on Saturday to start their fresh jobs at club level.

The trio will all join the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in the dugout at Old Trafford with it being reported that the Premier League outfit paid an additional fee to release them from their contracts with US Soccer, following the £7m outlay to secure Pochettino’s services.

The Athletic reports that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jr., immediately travelled to Manchester after the US’ 6-0 win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals at the weekend.

That was the first of their two-legged tie, but US Soccer allowed them to depart prematurely as a result of their aggregate lead being so great.

Pochettino will remain in-post for his final match in charge on Tuesday, when the US take on Haiti once more, this time in Cincinnati.

The 54-year-old will leave the US setup just three months after penning a latest four-year deal following the World Cup.

Miguel D’Agostino, who has been one of Pochettino’s longest-serving assistants, has remained with his manager for the second leg, but he is also expected to move to Old Trafford when Pochettino begins work officially on November 18, as was confirmed by United.

Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils will be a trip to Anfield on Sunday, as he looks to guide his upcoming side away from the relegation zone.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hideki Shirakawa pioneered the field of conductive polymers, overturning the common view that plastics do not conduct electricity. His demonstration that thin films of polyacetylene — an organic polymer — can become conductive when doped with small amounts of other chemicals earned him a share of the 2000 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (with Alan MacDiarmid and Alan Heeger). He was the second Japanese chemist to receive this award, after Kenichi Fukui in 1981. Shirakawa has died aged 90.

Shirakawa was born in Tokyo. After graduating from secondary school in Takayama City, he studied chemical engineering at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (now the Institute of Science Tokyo). He went on to pursue master’s and doctoral studies there, under the supervision of polymer chemist Shu Kambara, earning a Doctor of Engineering degree for his research on how blocks of organic molecules combine to form polymer chains.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

After completing his doctorate in 1966, Shirakawa was hired as a research associate in the laboratory of Sakuji Ikeda at Tokyo Tech. There, he began studying how acetylene molecules join together to form a polymer, using Ziegler–Natta catalysts (which are based on organic molecules containing transition metals).

In 1967, Shirakawa was joined in his experiments by a visiting researcher from South Korea, Hyung Chick Pyun. The pair were polymerizing acetylene using a catalyst composed of tetrabutoxytitanium and triethylaluminium to produce powdered polyacetylene.

Sources indicate that on one occasion, however, the protocol failed to produce the powder. Instead, a ragged film formed on the surface of the solution in the flask. On closer inspection, it became clear that the visiting researcher had mistakenly used a much higher concentration of the catalyst than was intended — 1,000 times higher. Shirakawa went on to synthesize a thin film of polyacetylene with a metallic lustre by introducing acetylene gas into a flask coated on the inside with the concentrated catalyst.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Subsequently, he travelled to the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, where he worked with MacDiarmid and Heeger. The team discovered that adding small amounts of molecules that accept electrons (such as bromine) or that donate electrons (such as arsenic pentafluoride) increased the electrical conductivity of the thin film by a factor of ten million. This work led to the trio’s Nobel award.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

In a recent development, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Thomas Frank succeeds Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager, signing a two-and-a-half-year deal with the south-east London club.

The Dane will be in the dugout for Palace’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, returning to management for the first time since leaving Tottenham in February.

Frank was on the Eagles’ shortlist to take over from Oliver Glasner this summer before they opted for Sage, and the former Spurs and Brentford boss is said to have been keen on a return to the Premier League.

After a difficult spell in north London, with the club sitting narrowly above the relegation zone when he left, Frank took time away from management to learn from leaders inside and outside football, as well as spending time with friends and family.

His disastrous stint at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has inevitably left some scars, but Frank is still widely revered for his work in the west of the capital, where he got the Bees promoted to the Premier League, stabilising them as a top-flight club on one of the division’s lowest budgets.

Frank will undoubtedly have learnt some lessons from his seven-month spell at Spurs.

Here, Sam Tabuteau identifies the three biggest mishaps of Frank’s Tottenham tenure….

Admitting Tottenham would ‘lose games’.

Part of what made Frank such an engaging character at Brentford was his ability to talk openly and honestly about the club’s culture, tactics and wider societal problems while maintaining an endearingly British sense of humour.

At times self-deprecating and sarcastic, Frank earned plenty of admirers for the way in which he humanised what can often be a cut-throat and emotionally vacant industry.

After nine years at Brentford, nearly seven as head coach, Frank had earned the luxury of being able to talk so candidly. He was comfortable in his surroundings, and safe in the knowledge that Brentford had not sacked a manager since 2015.

However, at Tottenham, he was starting from scratch at a club whose ambitions don’t leave much room for home truths.

Coming off the back of their Europa League triumph, Spurs supporters wanted to hear how the club was going to push forward.

Yet in his first press conference as Spurs manager, Frank joked that if there was one thing he could promise, it was that they would lose games.

Frank appointed upcoming Crystal Palace manager.

Frank’s first words as Palace manager as former Spurs boss appointed.

Arteta facing new Arsenal dilemma after inevitable Gyokeres goals.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

His ill-timed quip did not go down well, regardless of the spirit in which it was intended, and from that point on Frank was fighting a losing battle to convince supporters he understood the culture of the club.

Losing supporters after tame Chelsea defeat.

Given how it ended, Frank’s tenure started surprisingly positively, with Tottenham third in the Premier League table after nine games.

The mood quickly changed, though, after a dispiriting 1-0 home defeat to London rivals Chelsea, in which Spurs managed just one shot on target.

Frank’s pragmatic style worked well at Brentford because they had one of the most efficient frontlines in the division and were not expected to dominate possession.

At Spurs, however, Frank’s risk-averse style combined with an attacking unit missing Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison meant they relied heavily on set-piece goals and struggled to create chances in open play.

Frank’s inability to evolve his style, coupled with Spurs’ shortcomings in attack, culminated in a performance against Chelsea that left many supporters disillusioned and would come to symbolise his time in charge.

Another example of Frank’s naivety came during January’s stoppage-time defeat to Bournemouth, when the 53-year-old was pictured pre-match walking around the pitch at the Vitality Stadium with an Arsenal-branded coffee cup.

Seemingly none the wiser, Frank stood with the cup in hand while some staff members could not hide their shock, and the resulting pictures went viral as Spurs slumped to an excruciating defeat.

After the game, Frank’s blunder took centre stage, and his mystified reaction just about summed up the growing rift between him and Spurs’ supporters.

While Spurs fans vented their anger and embarrassment online and in the stands, Frank could not begin to understand how an innocent mistake could be blown so far out of proportion.

From that point on, it was clear that the narrative was rapidly beginning to slip from Frank’s grasp and Spurs would lose their next five league games before he was relieved of his duties.

What is the 3pm blackout? Could Premier League rule be scrapped after Andy Burnham comments?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.
  • The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would “urge caution” on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout, and called for broadcasters to be mindful of the impact on fans caused by changes to kick-off times.

The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.

The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.

Burnham noted any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

“I would urge a bit of caution on it (the blackout), because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs,” he remarked.

“If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

“So I think it has to be considered carefully. I’m not going to take the pure consumer view here. I’ll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue.

“I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying ‘let’s have even more live football’.

According to recent reports, “I think it’s about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those challenges matter to me, first of all.”.

The trend in television rights has been to offer more matches in order to keep revenues up – the current Premier League deal includes 270 live matches compared to 200 in the previous one for example.

The logical conclusion of that trend is for all matches to be made available live, and the SPFL’s tender for its next set of rights is reported to offer the chance to do just that.

The blackout is enforced by Article 48 of UEFA’s statutes, which the Football Association and the Scottish Football Association choose to impose.

It applies when 50 per cent or more of matches in the top two divisions are due to be played simultaneously.

It has been revealed that premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT in August that English football was leaning towards a blackout but added: “It’s not just us involved in the decision about Article 48. It’s us, the EFL and the FA.

“”We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

“It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

“I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”.

Burnham was also asked if broadcasters needed to be more mindful of the disruption caused to fans by the scheduling of matches for live broadcast.

“It doesn’t give any regard, actually, as far as I can see, to travelling supporters,” he mentioned.

“Monday night games, you know, people in the north-east coming to the north-west, it’s not fair, the way that is done, or very early kick-offs on Saturday, very difficult for people to get there. So on that, I agree (with the need to be more mindful).

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:32, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 12:34.

Crystal Palace are reportedly close to appointing Thomas Frank as their upcoming head coach.

The Eagles appear to be moving swiftly to replace Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

It had previously been reported that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage, while the likes of Anthony Barry, Vitor Pereira, Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss Frank has now been identified as the leading candidate to take the reins at Selhurst Park, with ‘advanced talks’ held over the weekend.

The Athletic have since claimed that Palace are finalising an agreement to appoint Frank, who is expected to become the club’s latest head coach.

Talks are remarked to be ongoing over Frank’s backroom staff and an official announcement of his arrival in South London is set to follow in due course.

All being well, Frank could potentially take charge of his first Crystal Palace game on Saturday when they travel to Coventry City in the Premier League.

If Frank is not appointed before the weekend, then the Dane could instead make his Palace debut in the Europa League when the Eagles play host to Real Sociedad on November 26.

The 53-year-old is set to return to management for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham in February after only eight months in charge.

Frank won just 13 of his 38 matches with Spurs and left the club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

He had previously enjoyed a successful seven-year spell as Brentford boss between 2018 and 2025, steering the Bees into the top flight and then establishing them as a competitive Premier League outfit, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

In June, Frank stated that he had no intentions to take a new managerial position, but he now appears to be ready to return to the dugout and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

Frank will be tasked with lifting the Eagles off the foot of the Premier League table following a run of seven defeats in 10 games at the start of this season under Sage, conceding a division-high 24 goals in the process.

However, victory over Coventry this weekend could see Palace climb out of the relegation zone and up to 16th in the table if other results were to go their way.

Thomas Frank has been confirmed as Crystal Palace’s newly introduced manager, with the Dane in post for the trip to Coventry this weekend.

He replaces Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week with Palace bottom of ther Premier League table.

Frank, who has been out of work since leaving Tottenham in February, was on Palace’s shortlist over the summer as they looked for a replacement for Oliver Glasner.

The Eagles ultimately agreed a three-year deal with Sage, but a disastrous start to the season saw the Frenchman relieved of his duties on Thursday.

The Dane has penned a two and a half year contract with the south Londoners, with club chairman Steve Parish hailing his “proven track record”.

“I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace,” Parish noted in the club announcement.

“He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”.

In his first words as Palace boss, Frank called his newly introduced side an “iconic club”.

According to recent reports, "It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

Sources indicate that "Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.”.

Frank endured a difficult spell at Spurs, who had been dragged into a relegation battle by the time he was sacked, but there remains a good deal of appreciation for his work at Brentford.

During his time in west London, Frank earned promotion to the Premier League before stabilising Brentford as a top-flight club and getting them challenging for Europe on one of the smallest budgets in the division.

Frank’s immediate task will be to drag Palace out of the relegation zone, starting with back-to-back fixtures against newly promoted Coventry and Hull.

Declan Rice notes the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and noted he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 13:21.

England have set a newly introduced all-time winning record after beating world champions Spain 3-2 in their final UEFA Nations League group fixture on Sunday.

The Three Lions knew that they had to beat the 2026 World Cup winners at Estadio Metropolitano on Madrid if they were to finish top of League A Group 3 on goal difference.

Thomas Tuchel’s side entered the half-time interval in front courtesy of a converted penalty from 2026 Ballon d’Or winner and England’s top goalscorer Harry Kane, who has set yet another scoring record.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased England’s lead with two goals in the space of just four minutes, putting the visitors firmly in control.

However, Elliot Anderson was sent off just six minutes after England’s third goal for a last-man pull-back on Lamine Yamal inside the penalty area, with Mikel Oyarzabal netting the resulting spot kick.

The momentum then shifted into Spain’s favour and substitute Nico Williams gave the hosts hope of a late comeback with a 75th-minute strike, but the Three Lions admirably dug deep to hold on for a crucial victory.

Victory for England means they have now won 10 consecutive away matches across all competitions for the first time in their history.

Success has also confirmed that England finish top of League A Group 3, progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals where they will face one of the runners-up in League A, with a guaranteed second leg at home.

Furthermore, England’s memorable night in Madrid saw them end Spain’s world-record 43-game unbeaten run spanning across almost three years.

After the match, Tuchel acknowledged that his team’s performance against La Roja was their best since he became England head coach in January 2025.

“Yes,” he told reporters. “Given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. That was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

In a recent development, “What a performance we put out there to be deservedly 3-0 up after 60 to 65 minutes. Of course the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes [of defending] against Spain in Spain feels like three hours!

“This was, of course, a statement victory and the statement and significance of it was that it was deserved.

In a recent development, “The result followed the performance. It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, on all aspects of the game.

“We did everything that needs to be done together – the deep buildup, the high press and attacking defensive phases.

England’s next match will be the first leg of their Nations League quarter-final tie, scheduled between March 25 and March 27 next year.

The Three Lions will discover their opponent when the draw is made on Friday at 11am UK time.

England cannot be drawn against Spain again, but they could face Group A1 runners-up Belgium, or one of three teams from Group A2 (Netherlands, Greece or Germany) or Group A4 (Portugal, Denmark or Norway).

The official quarter-final lineup will be confirmed after the final round of fixtures on Tuesday.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Recent findings suggest that before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night.

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his latest role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending new job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

In a recent development, ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he remarked. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Industry observers note that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Manchester United have been dealt a fresh blow in their pursuit of a left-back.

The Red Devils are worryingly short in that position, especially after injuries to both Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu this season.

It left now-sacked manager Michael Carrick to field right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui in that role in the absence of his two natural options.

It was one of a number of problems facing the former midfielder, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday after just one win in 11 games.

Mauricio Pochettino will take over the reins from him at Old Trafford, and the Argentine will look to stamp his mark on the United squad when it comes to recruitment.

Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall was a top target during the summer transfer window, but United did not act on that interest, with the former Chelsea defender penning a upcoming deal on Tyneside instead.

Now, the Press Association reports that the Magpies will not entertain any offers for the England international in the upcoming January transfer window.

He has established himself as Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice left-back in recent months, and he impressed against Lamine Yamal in the Three Lions’ shock 3-2 win over Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

It is thought that Newcastle are braced for more transfer interest in their 22-year-old, who signed for the north-east club in 2023, costing them £35million.

It is believed that they have no intention of selling him halfway through the campaign, having lost Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Alexander Isak in the space of two summer transfer windows.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage.

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

According to recent reports, ‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente mentioned when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’.

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’.

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the key tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’.

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Xavi attacked the mentality of his Netherlands squad after they fell to a humbling 5-0 loss against Germany in the Nations League on Monday.

Netherlands only needed a point to advance to the quarter-finals of the Nations League but suffered a heavy loss at the Olympiastadion that saw Germany win Group B.

Derry Scherhant's fine strike put Germany in front four minutes before half-time, and they added four goals in the space of 17 minutes during a frantic second-half period – Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda scoring either side of Florian Wirtz's second goal.

The result was a bitter pill for Xavi to swallow having seen his team defeat Greece 7-0 on Friday, and he blasted his players for their performance.

"First of all, we have to say sorry for the supporters because we were not playing football – no values, no spirit, no anything," Xavi told NOS.

"As a coach, I cannot understand because we played an incredible game against Greece, with the spirit, values, intensity and passion. This was completely the opposite.

"Maybe because I'm newly introduced here, and I'm still trying to understand the spirit of the players – maybe it's a lack of mentality as well.

"I was talking to them, they talked as well, so I think it's good that we have had the communication and now we know the scenario.

Recent findings suggest that "We have the capacity to do amazing things, but we did the complete opposite so it is a pity. I'm really disappointed, really sad because until [this match] I was really proud of the team, of the players – each one of them, but it was a shock for me as a coach.

According to recent reports, "We're going to build something starting from now. I talked to the players honestly that we need to change the mentality and the values they have on the pitch even if we win, draw or lose. But it was impossible to complete [when] playing without values.".

— OnsOranje (@OnsOranje) November 16, 2026.

Xavi did not feel the absences of star duo Virgil van Dijk and Frenkie de Jong played a role in the result.

The Netherlands boss added: "It was 99% because of the values.

According to recent reports, "It's embarrassing. We had the chances. We created things. We suffered because they played so well with the values that we wanted and that we had in the first five games.

"I'm trying to understand what happened, but it's difficult because three days ago we did an incredible game in terms of values and football-wise. But here the values were zero.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • England captain Harry Kane has etched his name into the record books once again after scoring in Sunday’s 3-2 triumph over Spain in the UEFA Nations League.
  • The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner made his 127th international appearance at Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, just three days after surpassing Peter Shilton as England’s most-capped player against Croatia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:20.

England captain Harry Kane has etched his name into the record books once again after scoring in Sunday’s 3-2 triumph over Spain in the UEFA Nations League.

The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner made his 127th international appearance at Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, just three days after surpassing Peter Shilton as England’s most-capped player against Croatia.

On the stroke of half time, Kane fired England into a deserved half-time lead with a converted penalty after being felled by Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

In doing so, England’s No.9 has now equalled an impressive scoring feat which had been unmatched since 1948.

Indeed, Kane has scored in each of his last seven international away matches dating back to June 2025, becoming the first Three Lions player to achieve this feat since legend Tom Finney between September 1946 and May 1948.

This record excludes neutral venues and therefore does not include the goals Kane scored at the 2026 World Cup where England finished third.

Kane’s away scoring streak began with goals in four successive World Cup qualifiers against Andorra, Serbia, Latvia and Albania, helping the Three Lions complete their qualification campaign with a perfect record.

The Bayern Munich striker has since netted in all three of his away matches with England in the Nations League against Czech Republic, Croatia and now Spain.

Kane has scored a total of 10 goals across those seven away games, while he has also extended his all-time scoring record with England to 93.

The last time Kane failed to make the net ripple for England at a non-neutral away venue came against Greece in November 2024 (3-0 Nations League win).

Kane will endeavour to surpass Finney outright and extend his scoring run on the road to eight games when England enter the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Reacting to England’s memorable win in Madrid, Kane told reporters: “I think that’s as big as it gets outside of a major tournament, for sure.

“We spoke before the Nations League campaign that we want to use these games to really improve, really stamp our identity on how we want to move going forward.

Sources indicate that “No better game than Spain away after they’re unbeaten in 40-odd games to show that, and what a performance. Up until the red card it was dominant, clinical, high intensity and they couldn’t live with it.

“It was a shame [Elliot Anderson’s] red card happened because I think [the scoreline] could have been more and that’s been our mindset. That it doesn’t matter what the scoreline is – we go and we go and we go. You saw that out there tonight.

“In the end, we had to find a different way to win with the red card, obviously, and it was similar to a Mexico feeling where we’re digging deep.

“But when you can do both sides of the game like that it means you’re a very good team, so credit to everyone involved. It’s been a great campaign so far and we can end the year with our heads held high.”.

Kane has scored in all six of England’s Nations League matches in the 2026-27 campaign, netting a competition-high eight goals in total to put him firmly in the frame to win the Golden Boot.

The Red Devils were on the hunt for a new manager after sacking Michael Carrick last week, with the former midfielder relieved of his duties after just one win in 11 matches.

It left the Premier League side mired in the top-flight relegation zone, and searching for their eighth permanent head coach since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

They turned to the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss after it became clear that he had a £7.5million release clause in his contract with US Soccer as head coach of the United States’ men’s side.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, formerly of Newcastle and Bayern Munich respectively, were publicly-known candidates for United, but the former was decided against without any further consideration, while the latter’s lack of Premier League experience ultimately went against him. The same could be noted for Stuttgart’s Sebastian Hoeness.

The Athletic claims that United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe held a personal interest in another ex-Chelsea and Tottenham figure, Antonio Conte, but the Italian’s desired level of control over club proceedings was believed to be ‘not the right fit’.

Como’s Cesc Fabregas, who masterminded the shock 4-1 victory over United in the Champions League earlier this term, was admired by chief executive Omar Berrada, but there were no further discussions over the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE.

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

Industry observers note that ‘There’s no number one,’ mentioned the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Industry observers note that speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

Industry observers note that ‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’.

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’.

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Naturally, attentions have rapidly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’.

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

Industry observers note that ‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’.

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’.

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:41.

Tottenham Hotspur are expected to accelerate their pursuit of a new striker during the January transfer window, according to a report.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side have struggled to convert chances so far this season, with only Sunderland (eight) and Nottingham Forest (nine) netting fewer goals than Spurs (10) in the Premier League after 10 games.

Spurs were unable to make the net ripple when they lost 1-0 at Leeds United before the international break, a result that ended a positive three-match winning run.

Dominic Solanke and summer signing Omar Marmoush have alternated leading the line under De Zerbi, but the pair have scored just three goals between them this season.

In fact, no Spurs player has scored more than two goals this term, with Solanke one of four men along with Conor Gallagher, Jan Paul van Hecke and Ben Davies who has netted multiple goals.

Spurs’ struggles in front of goal come at a time when Richarlison – the club’s top scorer with 11 PL goals last season – has been exiled from the senior squad after requesting to leave in the summer.

TEAMtalk reports that Bournemouth star Eli Junior Kroupi is a player ‘loved’ by De Zerbi, but his valuation between £80m and £100m could prove to be a major stumbling block for a club who spent in excess of £300m in the summer.

Spurs have since been on the lookout for alternative centre-forward options ahead of the New Year, with Freiburg frontman Igor Matanovic viewed as a possible target.

The 6ft 4in Croatia international has been in prolific form so far this season, scoring eight goals in 16 games across all competitions.

Journalist Ben Jacobs has revealed that Matanovic is indeed "one name" on Tottenham’s radar, but it remains to be seen whether they will push for the 23-year-old in January or wait until next summer.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs stated: “I think they could go for one [a striker] in January if the right target presents itself.

“It’s a shame how the Richarlison situation has panned out. Igor Matanovic is one name, as I exclusively revealed, that Tottenham like. They may look for something a little bit more short-term, like a loan. The same for Manchester United.

“If they can’t find the right target, or maybe someone with a bit more experience within the Premier League, then they can reassess in the summer.

“What they won’t want to do is necessarily go all in and panic buy in January for someone on a long-term contract, instead of just biding their time and waiting it out.”.

Spurs could face competition from Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United for Matanovic, who is believed to be valued in the region of £50m.

Freiburg are in no rush to part ways with Matanovic, who remains a key player and is under contract at the Bundesliga club until 2029.

Re-signing striker Will Lankshear from Middlesbrough has also been mooted for Spurs, but the Championship club have allegedly slapped a £70m price tag on the 21-year-old, just months after signing him in the summer for a deal worth up to £20m.
