In a recent development, during my graduate studies at the University of California, San Diego, long hours in the laboratory were often stressful, and not just because of the research. Most of my anxiety came from looking out the window at perfect surfing conditions and realizing I didn’t have much time to finish my experiments and leave while the ‘waves were firing’.

It has been revealed that several years on, I am now an assistant professor at the School of Ocean Futures at Arizona State University (ASU), working from Hilo, Hawaii, where I balance scientific research with my second job: travelling the world as a non-competitive professional surfer. Also known as a free surfer, I ride a variety of board designs — from conventional wooden surfboards to modern big-wave ‘guns’ — and produce social-media content, such as photos and videos, in exchange for endorsement opportunities.

My research is also deeply connected to the ocean. I study coral microbiomes, sampling the community of microorganisms living on and in the coral before and after environmental stress to improve understanding of reef health and the sea-bed formations that create waves, referred to as surf breaks. In May, my colleagues and I reported on the importance of creating a framework to analyse systems with environmental, social and cultural components to protect surf ecosystems1.

Recent findings suggest that in my faculty position, I work in nine-month appointments, and I am permitted to spend a number of work hours each calendar year on non-conflicting outside business. I spend roughly 85% of my work year on research and teaching and 15% on surfing assignments.

Sources indicate that many careers are no longer confined to a single discipline or identity, and some of the most meaningful work now happens at the intersection between different skills, communities and ways of thinking. Surfing shapes the questions I want to ask as a scientist, while science provides me with ways to understand and protect ocean environments. When I was a student, I used to worry that I would have to choose between surfing and science. Today, my career exists because I didn’t.

According to recent reports, when I graduated from high school in 2005, Native Hawaiians and Pacific Islanders made up less than 0.2% of all science, technology, engineering and mathematics degree graduates in the United States. Today, that number remains at only 0.3%2. As a Native Hawaiian kid, targeted fellowships and private programmes made university possible for me, covering my tuition and board.

In a recent development, after I started a PhD chemistry programme at the University of California, San Diego, in 2012, my studies became much more demanding. Courses, a teaching-assistant role, fellowship requirements and lab training would keep me on land from sunrise until sundown. Despite being able to see the ocean from nearly every window on campus, it was the time in my life that I felt furthest from it.

It has been revealed that remarkably, it was during the third year of my PhD programme that getting paid to surf actually became a reality. After many nights spent in the lab, I decided to set academic boundaries and rededicate time to the waves, mostly as a way to protect my mental health. I stopped measuring success only by hours in the lab. Instead, I treated time in the ocean as part of the scientific process.

Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?

Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?

Surfing-industry figures took notice, and not long after becoming more present on the beaches, I was offered modest ambassadorial contracts that developed into respectable budgets that let me travel to places with better waves and to collaborate with local board builders — when not in the lab, of course.

When I moved back to Hawaii in 2018, I received a US National Science Foundation postdoctoral fellowship for broadening participation of under-represented groups in biology and I began to use surfing as a vehicle for communicating coral science. That eventually led to Arizona State University recruiting me to join its Hilo-based Center for Global Discovery and Conservation Science in 2021, a position that has since evolved into my current role.

In a recent development, blending the two disciplines has made my research more creative and my surfing more meaningful. It also taught me the importance of protecting time for the parts of life that keep you grounded. Whether that be surfing, music, art or family, maintaining space for your passions is not a distraction from academic work; it is often the very thing that sustains it.

Here are some guiding principles that have helped me to navigate the worlds of surfing and academia.

Recent findings suggest that the best experiences come when you find a crew that wants to surf the same waves or explore the same questions as you. Some of the most important opportunities in my career came from relationships that started organically, often through time spent in the ocean and local communities, or through a shared curiosity, rather than formal networking.

In a recent development, the researchers, surfers, photographers and conservationists I work with are people who genuinely care about the places we study and the communities connected to them. Over time, those shared values create trust that later opens doors to research projects, publications, funding opportunities and creative collaborations. I’ve found that the best way to find these people is not by chasing status or connections but by consistently showing up in the communities and places that you genuinely care about.

Mauricio Pochettino is set to raid US Soccer as he continues to build his backroom staff at Manchester United.

The Argentine is set to take over the reins from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on Wednesday, having overseen the United States’ Concacaf Nations League quarter-final first and second legs against Haiti.

His side won 6-0 in their first match, and he will take charge of his final game on Tuesday before flying over to Manchester on Wednesday morning.

The Athletic reports that Pochettino’s assistants have already made their way over to England to begin work, with Toni Jimenez, Jesus Perez and his son Sebastiano Pochettino all beginning their fresh jobs at Carrington early.

Now, it looks as though the 54-year-old is not done finalising his support crew, with it believed that analyst Alec Scott will also join him in the north west.

Scott was already in-position with US Soccer before Pochettino arrived in 2024, but he has had such an impact on the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss that he wants to bring him to the Premier League with him.

Miguel D’Agostino, Pochettino’s long-serving assistant manager, has remained with the USMNT head coach for the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati, but he is also expected to join his colleague at United later this week.

Pochettino’s first game in charge will come this Sunday, when he oversees his upcoming side against Liverpool at Anfield.

United sit in the relegation zone in the English top flight after a run of one win in 11 matches.

Jurgen Klopp declared he fell in love with his Germany squad at first sight, as he heaped praise on their 5-0 destruction of the Netherlands in the Nations League on Monday.

The former Liverpool boss, appointed after the shock last-32 exit to Paraguay at the 2026 World Cup, assembled a huge 44-man squad for his first games in charge in September, splitting the group in two for their four matches.

Germany started slowly under Klopp and won just one of those fixtures – a 2-0 victory over Serbia – before the coach selected a standard 24-man squad for this international break which produced the goods.

After defeating Serbia 3-1 last Friday, they remarkably thrashed Xavi's Netherlands in Berlin to book their place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

In a recent development, "In the summer, you got the feeling that the upcoming coach, which was me, had to get drunk to make the German national team look good. But I arrived and was head over heels in love – with 44 men," Klopp told ARD.

"Those who are here now are wonderful footballers, great characters. But the perception from the outside was different.

"We have a good idea, and thought if we can get these highly talented players moving, it could work well; then it won't be fun to play against us.

"And now everyone will go home with a smile and won't question the national team for at least three or four months.

"Instead they will think, 'This could be something special'.".

Derry Scherhant curled his first international goal into the top corner just before half-time, before Florian Wirtz struck twice, with his goals coming either side of Nico Schlotterbeck's header.

Brajan Gruda impressed and he added to his pair of assists by rounding off the scoring with his second goal in as many international appearances.

Sources indicate that "The game was extraordinary, also exceptionally difficult. We scored incredible goals, it was just insane," said Klopp.

"A fantastic football match, a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have dared to wish for something like this.

"This is a very special group at the moment.

Sources indicate that "All problems have not been solved – that's nonsense, of course. But we have shown our potential. We have set the bar high for ourselves and we have to keep surpassing it.".

It has been revealed that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Martin Zubimendi is seriously considering leaving Arsenal for the first time and has refused to rule out a move to Chelsea, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game for Arsenal this season, with the concerning lack of game-time sparking speculation over his future at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spanish midfielder enjoyed a bright start to his Gunners career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad, earning rave reviews from Mikel Arteta this time last year.

But Zubimendi had lost his place in the Arsenal team by the end of the season, with a teenage Myles Lewis-Skelly instead starting the Champions League final against PSG.

The 27-year-old has continued to struggle for minutes this season and is now, for the first time, considering his future at the club.

Spanish outlet AS say Zubimendi has his eye on a January exit and is ‘open to everything’ following reports linking him with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

Xabi Alonso is keen to strengthen his midfield options and knows Zubimendi well from his previous spell at Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi is contracted to Arsenal until 2030 but reports in Spain say the north London club will consider offers for the World Cup winner of at least £60m.

Last week, Zubimendi was forced to address speculation linking him with a move away from Arsenal while on international duty with Spain.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

According to recent reports, ‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s swiftly forgotten and nothing happens.

‘I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’.

Zubimendi also revealed he was warned about a possible lack of minutes by Arteta ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

Arteta bolstered his midfield options over the summer, with Arsenal spending £75m to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,’ Zubimendi added. ‘As he does with all the players, he explained the blueprint to me.

‘He warned me that there were fresh signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

‘It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too. Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

‘I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very rapidly.’.

Jorginho has revealed that Chelsea's squad disagreed with BlueCo's decision to sack Thomas Tuchel in 2022.

Tuchel is at the moment receiving widespread plaudits after his England team ended Spain's 43-game undefeated streak on Sunday evening.

England stormed into a three-goal lead inside an hour, before an Elliot Anderson red card contributed to the Three Lions having to see out a nervy end to the contest in Madrid.

The result has helped Tuchel rebuild his reputation in significant games, but the German will forever regarded as a Chelsea legend after the club's Champions League triumph in 2021.

However, 15 months on from that success in Porto, Tuchel was sacked by Chelsea's new owners BlueCo.

Speaking on the 'Obi One Podcast' hosted by former Blues midfielder John Obi Mikel, Jorginho acknowledged that he and his teammates were left stunned by the decision.

Asked to describe the reaction of Chelsea's first-team squad and himself, Jorginho replied: "What?".

"Like this. We were like 'we didn't expect it'. We were not having the best results at that moment, but us, it was not the moment.

"So, everyone was a bit shocked, yes".

At the start of the 2022-23 campaign, Chelsea collected 10 points from their opening six matches in the Premier League.

However, it was a 1-0 defeat away in Dinamo Zagreb that led to Tuchel being sacked by BlueCo on the following morning.

BlueCo had only just signed known Tuchel favourite Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to become the club's newly introduced number nine.

Since that decision on September 7, 2022, it has since been suggested that BlueCo wanted to appoint their own head coach, the indication being that they did not want a manager chosen by predecessor Roman Abramovich to remain at the helm if they were not fully aligned in their relationship and club strategy.

Max Dowman has given Mikel Arteta a serious decision to make as the Arsenal star impressed once more on international duty.

The winger netted his first goal for England’s Under-21 side on Monday, as Lee Carsley’s side ran out 3-2 victors against France at Ashton Gate in Bristol.

His strike wrote him into the history books for his country, as he became the youngest ever goalscorer for the Under-21 team.

Dowman, 16, started off the right flank for the Young Lions, and he scored the third goal for the home side on a wet Monday evening.

He had his Arsenal team-mate Ethan Nwaneri inside him as the No10, with Tottenham’s Mikey Moore, on loan at FC Koln in Germany, on the left wing.

Divin Mubama, the Southampton striker, led the line while young Gunner Tommy Setford, who is spending the campaign on loan at Stevenage in League One, was between the sticks.

Dowman produced a stellar showing, capping off a well-crafted England goal as Harrison Armstrong seized upon a late mistake in the French backline, before squaring to the young forward to slot home into an unguarded net.

It follows on from his impressive display in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal last time out, where he was introduced for Amario Cozier-Duberry on the hour by Carsley.

While he could not find that elusive equaliser, he was bright in his substitute cameo on Friday.

It remains to be seen what role he could play in Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle United this weekend, before they host Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City at the Emirates Stadium next week.

Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

Although Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams managed to claw two back for this year's World Cup winners, England held on with a backs-to-the-wall effort in the closing stages, courtesy of a few fine saves from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

After England's victory, which called an end to Spain's historic 43-game unbeaten run, Bellingham was spotted celebrating with his model girlfriend Ashlyn inside the stadium.

Wearing a beaming smile, he went over to embrace both the 28-year-old American and his father Mark as the family soaked up the celebrations in the stands.

The Real Madrid superstar has largely kept his relationship with Ashlyn private since the pair were first linked in early 2025.

Jude Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashlyn Castro celebrate England's superb win over Spain.

The Real Madrid star then caught up with his dad Mark on a special night for the Bellinghams.

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California (@instagram/ashlyncastro).

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California who boasts over one million followers on Instagram, sharing fashion and beauty content online.

Spanish media waxed lyrical about Bellingham's display on the night, claiming he was 'determined to make a statement' at the stadium of Real Madrid's rivals Atletico.

Sources indicate that newspaper AS wrote: 'If anyone felt the match was crucial, it was Jude Bellingham. He stepped onto the Metropolitano pitch determined to make a statement, to impose his usual footballing and physical prowess.

'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'.

It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’.

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] major time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the five teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, as things currently stand, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position in Group A4 is still to be confirmed after they were humbled at home by Denmark in their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo unveiled his retirement from international football.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

Sources indicate that the group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, TBC.

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, TBC.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

Tech Report: Thomas Frank's Crystal Palace in-tray: Three major complications newly introduced Eagles boss must solve to avoid relegation

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 15:28.
  • Crystal Palace are closing in on the appointment of Thomas Frank as their new head coach, according to The Athletic, with the former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford boss expected to replace Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park.
  • Recent findings suggest that the 53-year-old faces an enormous challenge after Palace collected just seven points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them at the foot of the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 15:28.

Crystal Palace are closing in on the appointment of Thomas Frank as their new head coach, according to The Athletic, with the former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford boss expected to replace Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park.

Recent findings suggest that the 53-year-old faces an enormous challenge after Palace collected just seven points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them at the foot of the table. He has only a handful of days to work with his new squad before Saturday's trip to Coventry City, making an immediate improvement essential.

Frank has plenty of rebuilding to do after his difficult spell in north London, but his successful seven-year stint at Brentford offers encouragement.

Sports Mole looks at three priorities that should dominate his in-tray in the first few months.

Frank's most urgent task will be to address a defence that has conceded 24 goals in just ten Premier League matches, the worst record in the division. Palace have also shipped eight goals from set pieces, including four during their current run of four consecutive defeats.

It is a problem that predates Sage's arrival, having also troubled Oliver Glasner, but Frank has a reputation for organising competitive sides and could bring some much-needed structure. At Brentford, he alternated between a 3-5-2 and 4-3-3, with the former potentially straightforward to implement given Palace's familiarity with a back three.

Sources indicate that however, the personnel available to him remain a concern. Palace did not adequately replace Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi, while summer arrivals Takehiro Tomiyasu, Axel Disasi and 18-year-old Honest Ahanor have not necessarily provided the defensive stability required.

Recent findings suggest that disasi is a particularly interesting case. The Chelsea loanee has an opportunity to establish himself as a key figure, but Frank must decide whether he is the right partner for the existing defensive options or whether further recruitment is required.

According to recent reports, frank's Brentford teams were also particularly dangerous from dead-ball situations, ranking among the Premier League's best for set-piece expected goals during his time there. Bringing that same attention to detail to both boxes could make an immediate difference.

Industry observers note that adam Wharton's decline in influence has been another major frustration for Palace. Only a few months ago, the midfielder was attracting reported interest from Chelsea, Manchester City and Liverpool, having established himself as one of the most exciting young English players in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that now, the noise surrounding his future has quietened considerably. Wharton missed out on England's 2026 World Cup squad and has struggled to reproduce the performances that previously made him so highly rated.

His average performance rating has dropped from fourth-best among Palace players in 2025-26 to seventh this season, with his contribution in possession and defensive work both coming under scrutiny.

Some of those difficulties appear connected to the unfamiliar responsibilities he has been given under Sage. Wharton has struggled to track runners and protect the space in front of the defence, and while not known for his attacking prowess, his influence in transition and in the final third has waned, registering fewer accurate long balls and key passes per 90 in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that frank must find a role that allows the 22-year-old to dictate games without leaving him exposed defensively. Restoring Wharton's confidence and getting him closer to his previous level would represent a significant boost, both for Palace's survival hopes and his longer-term development.

Palace's problems in front of goal are not quite as severe as their defensive shortcomings, but Frank will need to address the uncertainty surrounding his centre-forward options.

Jean-Philippe Mateta wanted to leave during the summer and is approaching the final months of his contract, while an injury has already disrupted his campaign. The Frenchman has yet to score in the Premier League this season and has accumulated more red cards than goals, leaving his future increasingly uncertain.

In a recent development, jorgen Strand Larsen has also struggled to convince since arriving, managing just one goal in eight league appearances. His record of 19 goals in 79 top-flight outings hardly suggests he is ready to become a reliable long-term replacement for Mateta.

Industry observers note that frank may therefore need to look beyond Selhurst Park when the January window opens. A reunion with Richarlison, who looks to be available from ex-club Spurs, is one possibility worth considering, particularly given the Brazilian's previous experience under the Dane.

In a recent development, palace spent heavily on 11 summer arrivals, so chairman Steve Parish may be reluctant to sanction another significant recruitment drive. Nevertheless, losing Mateta without securing a dependable replacement would leave Frank with a major problem.

With Palace already facing a fight to climb away from the bottom of the table, Frank cannot afford to wait until January to make improvements.

Defensive organisation, Wharton's revival and a reliable goalscorer represent three clear priorities if he is to turn a troubled season around.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Thomas Frank described Crystal Palace as an "iconic club" and vowed to turn their fortunes around after being announced as the Eagles' fresh manager.

Frank was appointed as Pierre Sage's successor on Monday after the Frenchman was dismissed during the international break with Palace at the bottom of the Premier League.

The 53-year-old is back in management nine months on from his tumultuous stint with Tottenham, which ended with the club sitting just outside the relegation zone.

Frank, who has penned a deal through to the end of the 2028-29 season, had been linked with the Palace job in the summer after Oliver Glasner left for Nottingham Forest.

It was also reported that Fulham were interested in his services, only to opt for Alvaro Arbeloa, while Sage was preferred to take the reins at Palace.

Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic and Ole Werner were all viewed as potential candidates to replace Sage.

But Palace have chosen to go with Frank, who will be the third manager to take charge of three different London clubs in the Premier League after Alan Pardew (Charlton Athletic, Crystal Palace, West Ham) and Harry Redknapp (Queens Park Rangers, Spurs, West Ham).

In a recent development, "It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it," Frank told Palace's official website.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League.

"I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.".

First day complete Thomas Frank is in the building. https://t.co/6XDUexHQT7.

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 16, 2026.

Frank impressed during a seven-year stint with Brentford, winning 41.8% of his 317 games in charge of the Bees (W132 D77 L108).

However, he was unable to replicate that with Spurs, averaging just 1.12 points per game with the club in the Premier League (29 points in 26 games) and accumulating a win rate of 34.2% (P38 W13 D11 L14).

Despite Frank's struggles at Spurs, Palace chairman Steve Parish believes his experience of managing in the Premier League made him a "perfect fit" for the Eagles.

"I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace," Parish stated.

"He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

"I'm confident Thomas' extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.".

Frank will lead Palace out for the first time this Saturday in a clash against Lampard's Coventry City.

Fabregas is regarded as one of the brightest young coaches in world football, with the 39-year-old hugely impressive since taking charge of Como.

The former midfielder has won 46, drawn 26 and lost 26 of his 98 matches in charge of Como since being appointed permanent head coach in July 2024.

The Italian club's fourth-placed finish in the 2025-26 Serie A campaign saw them qualify for this season's Champions League, and they have impressed in the competition this term, including a standout 9-1 victory over Lille last time out.

Como are currently fourth in the Serie A table, only six points behind the leaders Lazio, and the team's style of football under Fabregas has been excelllent.

Man United lost 4-1 to Como in the Champions League earlier this season, and it appears only a matter of time before Fabregas makes the move to a major club.

According to The Athletic, Fabregas' name was mentioned when Man United had an executive committee meeting on November 5.

The report claims that Man United CEO Omar Berrada is a huge fan of Fabregas and had seemingly pushed the Spaniard's name into the conversation.

However, talk on Fabregas 'did not develop into anything further', according to the publication, with the club ultimately switching their attention to Mauricio Pochettino.

Fabregas has a contract with Como until the summer of 2028, and his future is certainly one to watch given how impressive his team have been.

Pochettino will officially become Man United's new head coach on November 18, once his commitments with USA have concluded.

The Argentine's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions will be Sunday's meeting with Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was declared that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andorra owner Gerard Pique notes Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was declared that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It promptly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he remarked in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’.

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’.

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’.

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend.

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Sources indicate that some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

According to recent reports, ‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

According to recent reports, ‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’.

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season.

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1322 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Climate change is affecting many types of crop, including these unusually small potatoes.Credit: John Thys/AFP/Getty.
  • Recent findings suggest that policymakers at the United Nations COP31 climate conference that started this week in Antalya, Turkey, will know that the UN Environment Programme has confirmed that global warming will exceed the limit of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial temperatures agreed in 2015 in Paris.
  • According to recent reports, there was a time — not that long ago — when many considered biotechnologies a threat to the environment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Climate change is affecting many types of crop, including these unusually small potatoes.Credit: John Thys/AFP/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that policymakers at the United Nations COP31 climate conference that started this week in Antalya, Turkey, will know that the UN Environment Programme has confirmed that global warming will exceed the limit of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial temperatures agreed in 2015 in Paris. This meeting comes hot on the heels of the UN COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, which affirmed yet again that the world is also in the middle of a biodiversity crisis. Progress in each case, whether preventing dangerous climate change or stemming biodiversity loss, is too slow. But researchers across scientific disciplines are now arguing that advances in biotechnology could provide solutions1. Methods such as gene editing and germplasm mining — the analysis of huge libraries of plant-genome sequences to find useful traits for crop improvement — can now be used to tackle global warming and protect nature, scientists write in a climate-themed issue of Nature Biotechnology.

According to recent reports, there was a time — not that long ago — when many considered biotechnologies a threat to the environment. But as the special issue reveals, a shift is under way. Now, the field offers strategies for protecting both climate and biodiversity from the many damaging effects of industrial agriculture.

Sources indicate that to feed a growing global population, between 2015 and 2024, the amount of cultivated land grew by roughly eight million hectares a year1. Yet, if the greenhouse-gas emissions, and thus global warming, this expansion causes is to be avoided, the world must work out how to produce enough food within its current agricultural footprint. Land clearance and land-use change contributes up to five billion tonnes of carbon annually — and is a major cause of biodiversity loss. Here, biotech solutions have some of the greatest potential, for example, by helping to increase crop yields and to protect plants from heat, drought and disease.

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze.

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze.

Sources indicate that of 77 such technologies with applications in agriculture, aquaculture and other sectors, many are ready for large-scale testing in the field, propose bioengineers Shekhar Mishra, Lauren Lui and Adam Arkin at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in California in a Perspective article2. Argentina, China and the United States have given the green light to engineered drought-tolerant crops.

Rice farming produces around 9% of human-caused emissions of the greenhouse gas methane. Now, researchers have found a way to slash these emissions, write agronomist Yunkai Jin at Hunan Agricultural University in Changsha, China, and his colleagues in a Comment article3.

But technological readiness isn’t enough: governments, regulators and the public need to be ready, too4. Readers might have a sense of déjà vu: in the 1990s, advances in biotechnology promised a revolution in food and agriculture — which subsequently stalled. The ambition was to genetically modify crops or engineer them in other ways so that they could tolerate herbicides, resist insects and fight viruses. But, at the time, many scientists, governments and corporations promoting the technology gave insufficient attention to several complications.

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.

Industry observers note that one concern was public anxiety about the idea of eating food produced using transgenic technologies — crops modified by inserting a gene from another plant species or other organism. Another concern was that risks to the environment and to human health had not been studied sufficiently. A third problem was that multinational companies dominated both the research and the development of these technologies, creating fears that the rise of agricultural biotechnology would put many small family farms out of business.

Sources indicate that environmental groups found common cause with consumer organizations. Together, they urged governments to enact strict regulations. In the European Union, for example, risks to human health and the environment needed to be assessed before technologies producing genetically modified organisms could be commercialized. Although this was necessary, it slowed down advances in low- and middle-income countries, because any nation intending to export produce to the EU would have to prove that it was not genetically modified.

Since then, at least two things have changed, increasing optimism about the use of biotechnology to help the planet. The discovery of gene editing — in which an organism’s genes are modified precisely to produce specific traits — has proved transformational for agriculture. The method is being developed cautiously and is regulated in a more nuanced way than were conventional technologies that produce genetically modified crops. In June, the EU amended its regulations on genetic modification and now permits the cultivation of some gene-edited crops.

‘Do I think Dalot is Denis Irwin? No. Let’s be really clear, Denis Irwin is the greatest full-back Manchester United have ever had, I shouldn’t be mentioning him in the same breath, but I would get rid of a few before Dalot,’ Neville remarked on Stick to United.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

In a recent development, the group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents will be revealed on Tuesday night, but as things at the moment stand, they could be drawn against either Portugal, Denmark or Norway.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

Liverpool are reportedly showing a keen interest in signing Brazilian youngster Arthur Dias.

Dias has graduated from Athletico Paranaense's youth system and has made 55 senior appearances since breaking into the first team last year.

The 19-year-old has featured 37 times during the current season, and his impressive performances have attracted the attention of Liverpool and several other heavyweight clubs.

Tottenham Hotspur reportedly made an attempt to sign Dias during the summer transfer window, submitting an offer worth around £16.6m, but their pursuit proved unsuccessful.

According to a report from Fussballeuropa, Spurs retain their interest alongside Liverpool, although Athletico-PR could demand a fee in the region of £25m for their prized asset.

Liverpool have sent scouts to watch him in recent matches as they continue to monitor the highly rated youngster's progress.

Aside from the two Premier League clubs, La Liga champions Barcelona are also in the race and have reportedly scouted him on several occasions.

There is also considerable interest from Germany, with Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig understood to be weighing up moves for the defender in January.

The Reds should be looking to recruit a newly introduced centre-back next summer, with Joe Gomez potentially heading for the exit door.

With Virgil van Dijk still performing at a high level, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in more young defensive talent and gradually develop them into potential successors to the Dutchman.

Liverpool have also been linked with a move for former defender Jarell Quansah, although it would likely take a substantial offer to bring him back to Anfield.

There is little harm in building a pool of exciting young defenders at the club, but whether Liverpool would be prepared to pay £25m for Dias remains to be seen.

“I am ready [to return],” he said. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he mentioned, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’.

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

Industry observers note that “But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel had mentioned he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

It has been revealed that proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

Recent findings suggest that and then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

It has been revealed that yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

Sources indicate that england had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

It has been revealed that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

It has been revealed that spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Recent findings suggest that pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

Recent findings suggest that england got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

Industry observers note that the referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

Industry observers note that there were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Recent findings suggest that eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

According to recent reports, kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

In a recent development, but then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Sources indicate that now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

In a recent development, spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

Industry observers note that in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

In a recent development, could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of newly introduced signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

According to recent reports, in the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Sources indicate that did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

Barcelona have released a statement confirming that Pau Cubarsi picked up an injury during Spain's UEFA Nations League contest with England on Sunday night.

Cubarsi started the clash with the Three Lions but was substituted at the half-time break.

Barcelona have revealed that the centre-back has strained his hip flexor, but it is unclear at this stage of proceedings how long the 19-year-old could be on the sidelines.

Industry observers note that “First-team player Pau Cubarsi has ​​a strain in his iliopsoas muscle. His availability for the match against Villarreal will depend on his recovery," read a statement from Barcelona.

Cubarsi has not yet been ruled out of Barcelona's La Liga clash with Villarreal on Sunday, but he is a doubt at this stage of proceedings.

The defender has been a vital player for Barcelona during the 2026-27 campaign, making 13 appearances in all competitions, providing two assists in the process.

Cubarsi will now not be in action with Spain until March, when the Nations League quarter-finals take place, with his full focus in the months ahead therefore set to be on Barcelona.

After the clash with Villarreal, Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with an away fixture against Sabah on November 25.

Barcelona will then finish the move away to Deportivo La Coruna in La Liga, before beginning December with a clash against Atletico Madrid on December 2.

Hansi Flick's side beat Atletico 2-1 when the pair last met on November 8.

Jules Kounde remains on the sidelines through injury, and he is unlikely to be unavailable for the clash against Villarreal this weekend.

However, Eric Garcia made his return from a muscular injury against Atletico as a second-half substitute, and the Spain international will likely replace Cubarsi in the starting side against Villarreal, should the latter be unavailable for selection.

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 17:14.

Manchester United will reportedly need to pay a handsome fee to sign Fulham defender Calvin Bassey during the January transfer window.

Mauricio Pochettino is keen to shore up United's leaky defence, and Bassey has emerged as a strong candidate to strengthen his backline.

The centre-back has made more than 110 appearances for the Cottagers across all competitions, scoring four goals, and has featured nine times in the Premier League this season.

The Red Devils have been monitoring the 26-year-old for some time, and Pochettino's arrival has further strengthened the case for pursuing his signature.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United would need to pay a fee in the region of £40m to bring Bassey to Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

Alvaro Arbeloa is keen for Bassey to commit his future to the club, and the Cottagers could potentially demand as much as £50m for their key centre-back.

Bassey's contract runs until the end of the season, and although Fulham have the option to extend it by another year, negotiations over a new deal have not progressed as smoothly as the club would have hoped.

The report claims that the former Rangers defender would be more than open to the prospect of moving to Old Trafford, which could work in Man Utd's favour.

Bassey would be an excellent addition to the squad and, in theory, should fit perfectly into Pochettino's system.

Pochettino typically favours an aggressive high defensive line, with pace and recovery speed essential qualities for his defenders, and Bassey certainly fits that profile.

Furthermore, the Nigerian international has considerable Premier League experience under his belt, while the reported asking price should fall within Man Utd's budget.

Bassey is also versatile enough to operate at left-back, which would be a major boost for Pochettino as the Red Devils look to provide cover for Luke Shaw.

A long overdue win at Anfield was marked by a goal, a number of other Arsenal chances, and what will go down as a famous clean sheet, all involving how the two teams defend at the back post.

There were plenty of other interesting things to note on Sunday – Martin Odegaard’s role drifting across the pitch early on and Arsenal’s 20-odd minute spell of dominance midway through the second half both caught the eye – but in the latest instalment of our video series Between The Lines, I look into how Arsenal had great joy attacking the back post, and why Liverpool were never going to have the same luck at the other end.

Recent findings suggest that with the hosts’ defence getting narrow in their own box, Arsenal created plenty of opportunities by having the man on the far side outside that defensive block. That’s how Kai Havertz scored, it’s how he nearly tapped in from Bruno Guimaraes’ effort that flew just wide, and it’s how Noni Madueke nearly teed Havertz up with another tap-in. It’s also where Christos Tzolis was positioned as he came onto a Madueke cross and forced Alisson into the game’s standout save.

Arsenal, though, have no such weakness: their combination of organisation, hunger, and (perhaps most importantly) focus meant Liverpool were never likely to find a spare man at the back post.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.

Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.

Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.

The Magpies star sparked a major police operation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir outside Newcastle, with at least six patrol cars joining the search for the £30million player.

After tracking down and questioning the Bosnian, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public and that the equipment was intended for recreational use.

But Dedic's escapade was certainly not the first time a footballer has found himself in hot water over the possession, carrying or use of a weapon, with brass knuckles, meat cleavers and BB guns among the bizarre arsenal of items to have attracted the authorities' attention over the years.

Marcus Bent, with a meat cleaver, in Surrey.

Former Middlesbrough and Everton forward Marcus Bent was tasered in his own home by police after threatening armed police officers with a meat cleaver and kitchen knife while under the influence of cocaine.

Bent, who avoided jail in 2016 after he pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine and affray, called Surrey Police after thinking he had discovered an intruder in his home.

Officers arrived at the scene but were initially unable to gain access to the property. Guildford Crown Court heard how the officers were about to use a battering ram to gain entry when a bare-chested Bent 'flung' open the door holding two chef's knives, with his 'eyes wide, jaw clenched and his body rigid'.

Industry observers note that bent, who was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, later said: 'I was paranoid and I was hallucinating. I felt there were people in my house. I remember thinking the door handle was moving.

According to recent reports, 'At no point was I ever going to take someone's life. I called them because I was hallucinating, paranoid, terrified.'.

Marcus Bent arrives at court before pleading guilty to possession of cocaine and affray.

Ashley Cole, with an air rifle, in Cobham.

To most, Ashley Cole is England's all-time greatest full-back but the three-time Premier League winner also made headlines for an infamous training ground air rifle incident.

Back in 2011 while playing for Chelsea, Ashley Cole accidentally shot and injured 21-year-old student Tom Cowan, who was on work experience at the Blues' training ground in Cobham, Surrey.

The Champions League winning left-back was reportedly 'larking about' with a .22 air rifle and accidentally shot Cowan from just five feet away.

The student had assumed he would get an invaluable experience on his brief visit to Cobham but instead had to be treated by medics and rest for the remainder of the day after the shot was fired.

Cole accidentally shot a 21-year-old on work experience at Chelsea's training ground.

Darren Bent, with a BB Gun, in Kesgrave.

Ex-England star Darren Bent ran into trouble early in his career when he was questioned over the alleged shooting of a 12-year-old boy with a ball-bearing gun.

While starring for his boyhood club Ipswich at the age of 20 in May 2004, Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause violence, before he was placed on bail and eventually released without charge pending further investigations.

According to a Suffolk Police statement at the time, a 12-year-old boy at a play area in Kesgrave had been struck in the back by a pellet from a ball-bearing gun (BB Gun). The incident was reported to authorities by his mother.

Bent, who was given a formal caution for his actions, went on to enjoy a fruitful career in the Premier League, representing the likes of Charlton, Tottenham, Sunderland and Aston Villa while also winning 13 caps for the Three Lions.

Early on his career Premier League legend Darren Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm.

Karim Adeyemi, with brass knuckles, in Germany.

The only member of this list to still be playing is Germany and Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi who was fined £396,000 in 2025 for possessing a pair of brass knuckles.

The former Borussia Dortmund forward was caught with the knuckles back in 2024, at the age of 22, but had to wait until the following year to receive his punishment.

Industry observers note that under German law the possession, procurement and use of brass knuckles is prohibited. The young winger avoided a public trial and a criminal record and was given a fine consisting of 60 daily payments of £6,600.

Although he never used the weapon, the German was in hot water  as he briefly lost his starting place in the German national team and at Borussia Dortmund.

The Westphalia giants released a statement saying: 'BVB always takes criminal allegations seriously and uses them as an opportunity to discuss them with its employees while respecting confidentiality obligations.'.

Adeyemi was lucky to dodge prison time after being charged with the possession of brass knuckles.

Diego Maradona, with an air rifle, in Buenos Aires.

Argentina icon Diego Maradona caused injuries to four people when he fired an air rifle at journalists and photographers while hiding behind a parked Mercedes outside his Buenos Aires home in February 1994.

Four years later, Maradona was found guilty of assault with a weapon and given a suspended prison sentence of two years and ten months, which was later reduced to an even two years.

To many he is the best of all time but Diego Maradona is hardly infallible off the pitch.

Despite appealing against the sentence which they claimed was 'too light', the journalists injured by Maradona said the verdict at least demonstrated there was 'justice for all' in Argentina.

'At least this exemplary case does show that there is justice for all,' remarked Daniel Talamoni, one of the four reporters who sued the World Cup winner.

Recent findings suggest that 'When the case began four years ago, everyone remarked it was impossible. They would sentence a man idolised in Argentina and forgive everything.'.

Arda Turan, with an unlicensed gun, in a Turkish hospital.

Sources indicate that keen fans of European football will not need to be reminded of who Arda Turan is. But they may be surprised to learn that the former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona star has had some serious trouble with the law.

Turan somehow avoided a jail sentence after discharging an unlicensed firearm in a hospital.

In 2018 while on loan from Barcelona in his home country of Turkey at Istanbul Basaksehir, Turan got into an altercation with Turkish singer Berkay Sahin, who ended in hospital with a broken nose.

Then Turan turned up at the hospital that was treating Sahin with an unlicensed firearm, and fired a shot into the floor.

Sources indicate that he was eventually sentenced to two years and eight months behind bars for firing a gun to cause panic, illegal possession of weapons and intentional injury but the sentence was suspended for five years. Basaksehir also fined the midfielder £350,000 over the incident.

Nearly a decade after the incident, Turan now manages Ukrainian powerhouse Shakhtar Donetsk, joining the club in May of last year.
